templates.title: squad recharge
templates.description: Their friend group came through for them — good laughs, good plans, the kind of hangout that left them feeling full instead of drained.

waysIn.title: Respect their social circle
waysIn.description: Let them keep the friend-time glow going, don't compete for their attention, just celebrate that they have people who show up for them.
waysIn.action: Ask about the funniest thing that happened during their hangout.

templates.title: someone had their back
templates.description: A friend really came through for them when it mattered, and it clearly meant more to them than they're saying out loud.

waysIn.title: Notice who shows up for them
waysIn.description: This isn't about you stepping in, it's about recognizing that their people matter to them too, and that's a good thing.
waysIn.action: Tell them you're glad they have someone like that in their corner.

templates.title: beef officially squashed
templates.description: They patched things up with a friend after some tension, and there's real relief in how much lighter they seem now that it's resolved.

waysIn.title: Let the relief land
waysIn.description: They just carried something heavy and set it down, give them room to feel good about it instead of picking it apart.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels now that things are okay again.

templates.title: real ones only
templates.description: They had one of those conversations with a friend that goes past the surface, the kind that reminds them why that friendship matters.

waysIn.title: Let them have their people
waysIn.description: This isn't your moment to compete with, it's a sign their support system is strong, which is good for both of you.
waysIn.action: Ask what they talked about that stuck with them.

templates.title: old friends, new memories
templates.description: They reconnected with someone from their past, and it brought back a version of them that's fun to see resurface.

waysIn.title: Get curious about their history
waysIn.description: Their old friendships are part of their story, showing interest in that side of them makes them feel fully known.
waysIn.action: Ask them to tell you a memory from back then that made them laugh.

templates.title: left off the group chat
templates.description: Their friends made plans without them, and it's been sitting heavier than they're letting on, even if they brushed it off out loud.

waysIn.title: Be the plan
waysIn.description: They don't need a pep talk about their friends, they need to feel chosen, be the one who shows up without being asked.
waysIn.action: Plan something just the two of you, no explanation needed, just make it happen.

templates.title: friendship on pause
templates.description: They got into it with a friend, and it's clearly still weighing on them even though they haven't said much about it.

waysIn.title: Don't force the debrief
waysIn.description: They might not be ready to unpack what happened, being available without pushing for details is more helpful than any advice.
waysIn.action: Let them know you're around if they want to talk it through, then drop it.

templates.title: stood up, kind of
templates.description: A friend bailed on plans they were looking forward to, and it stung more than they're admitting.

waysIn.title: Turn the letdown around
waysIn.description: The easiest fix isn't a conversation, it's an alternative, give them something else to look forward to instead of a lecture on flaky friends.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing the thing they had planned, just the two of you, instead.

templates.title: friendship on slow fade
templates.description: They've noticed a friendship quietly fading, less texting, less effort, and it's leaving a small ache they haven't fully named.

waysIn.title: Let them feel it without fixing it
waysIn.description: This one doesn't need solving, it needs acknowledging, sometimes friendships just change and that's allowed to be a little sad.
waysIn.action: Ask if they've talked to that friend, gently, no follow-up needed.

templates.title: trust took a hit
templates.description: A friend did something that broke their trust a little, and they're more guarded about it than they're showing.

waysIn.title: Be the safe one
waysIn.description: When trust gets shaken elsewhere, what helps most is knowing at least one relationship is solid, don't add more to prove it, just be consistent.
waysIn.action: Check in without bringing up the friend directly, just make things easy for them.

templates.title: insta bestie unlocked
templates.description: They met someone new and the chemistry was instant, that rare "we're friends now" energy from minute one.

waysIn.title: Get hyped with them
waysIn.description: New friend crushes hit different, let them gush about it without side-eyeing how fast they're calling someone a friend.
waysIn.action: Ask when they're hanging out with the new friend again.

templates.title: circle expansion arc
templates.description: They've been putting themselves out there and it's working, new faces, new energy, proof that leveling up their social life pays off.

waysIn.title: Clap for the courage
waysIn.description: Making new friends as an adult takes actual guts, acknowledge that instead of treating it like no big deal.
waysIn.action: Ask what made them want to branch out and meet new people.

templates.title: mutual friend jackpot
templates.description: A mutual friend put them onto someone new, and it turned into an actual connection instead of just a group chat add.

waysIn.title: Let the network do its thing
waysIn.description: This one's low-stakes and fun, no need to dig deep, just enjoy that their world is getting a little bigger.
waysIn.action: Ask how they met, mutual-friend stories are always good ones.

templates.title: internet friend, now real friend
templates.description: An online connection finally became a real one, and meeting up in person hit different than they expected, in the best way.

waysIn.title: Make the jump feel worth it
waysIn.description: Turning an online friendship into a real one takes trust, let them know that instinct paid off.
waysIn.action: Ask what surprised them most about meeting in person.

templates.title: vibe check: pending
templates.description: They tried to connect with someone new and it just didn't click the way they hoped, more awkward silence than easy conversation.

waysIn.title: Remind them it's not a verdict
waysIn.description: One awkward first meet doesn't mean anything about them, some connections just take more than one try, or don't happen, and that's fine.
waysIn.action: Ask lightly how it went, then let it go if they don't want to dwell on it.

templates.title: left on read, socially
templates.description: They put themselves out there trying to build something new, and got quietly ghosted instead of a real response.

waysIn.title: Let the sting be small
waysIn.description: Being ghosted by a potential friend stings more than people admit, don't minimize it, just be steady until it fades.
waysIn.action: Distract with something fun instead of analyzing why the other person went quiet.

templates.title: new place, no people yet
templates.description: They're in a new environment and still haven't found their people there, and the loneliness of that is starting to show.

waysIn.title: Be the familiar thing
waysIn.description: When everything around them is unfamiliar, being the one constant matters more than any advice about making friends.
waysIn.action: Plan something that makes them feel less alone in the new place, even something small.

templates.title: one-sided friendship energy
templates.description: They've been putting in the effort with someone new and it's not coming back the same way, and it's starting to feel discouraging.

waysIn.title: Notice the effort even if they didn't
waysIn.description: They don't need to be told to stop trying or to try harder, they need someone to notice they've been trying at all.
waysIn.action: Point out something specific they did to build that friendship, unprompted.

templates.title: family group chat, but IRL
templates.description: Their family pulled together for some quality time, and the chaos-but-loving energy of it clearly left them in a good mood.

waysIn.title: Get the family recap
waysIn.description: Family stories are usually the best ones, ask for the highlight reel instead of a generic "how was it."
waysIn.action: Ask for the funniest or most chaotic thing that happened.

templates.title: family showed up big
templates.description: A family member really came through for them, and having that kind of backup clearly meant a lot, even if they're playing it cool.

waysIn.title: Notice their support system
waysIn.description: This isn't about competing with family support, it's a good sign their world has multiple people in their corner.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's great they have that kind of family behind them.

templates.title: main character in the family group chat
templates.description: Their family celebrated something big with them, and being seen and celebrated by the people who've known them longest hits different.

waysIn.title: Add your own celebration on top
waysIn.description: Family already made them feel special, add to that instead of trying to top it, this one's easy.
waysIn.action: Ask them to relive the moment, what part felt the best.

templates.title: family beef: resolved
templates.description: They smoothed things over with a family member after some distance, and there's real relief in having that tension gone.

waysIn.title: Let the peace sit
waysIn.description: They just resolved something that's probably been sitting with them for a while, let them enjoy the lightness instead of asking for the backstory.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels now that things are smoothed over.

templates.title: family static
templates.description: They got into it with a family member, and it's clearly still sitting with them more than they're letting on.

waysIn.title: Don't force the debrief
waysIn.description: Family conflict is heavy and complicated, being a steady, low-pressure presence matters more than advice or opinions about who's right.
waysIn.action: Let them know you're around if they want to vent, no follow-up questions needed.

templates.title: family expectations, loading
templates.description: Family pressure has been weighing on them, comparisons, expectations, or just the feeling of never quite measuring up.

waysIn.title: Be their pressure-free zone
waysIn.description: They're getting enough pressure elsewhere, make this relationship the one place they don't have to perform or explain themselves.
waysIn.action: Remind them, plainly, that they don't have to prove anything to you.

templates.title: family duty, no days off
templates.description: Family responsibilities have been piling up on them, and the obligation of it all is starting to feel heavier than they're saying.

waysIn.title: Take something off their plate
waysIn.description: They don't need sympathy about family duty, they need one less thing to carry, even briefly.
waysIn.action: Offer to handle something small and unrelated so they have one less thing to manage.

templates.title: carrying something heavy
templates.description: Something difficult happened with their family, a loss or a hard health update, and they're carrying more weight than they're showing on the surface.

waysIn.title: Just be there, without fixing
waysIn.description: This isn't a moment for advice or silver linings, it's a moment to simply be present and let them lead on what they need.
waysIn.action: Check in gently and let them set the pace, don't push for details.

templates.title: in-law era: unlocked
templates.description: Time with their partner's extended family actually felt easy, less performing and more just genuinely enjoying being around them.

waysIn.title: Let the good vibes carry over
waysIn.description: This one's a nice full-circle moment, mirror that warmth instead of downplaying how well things are going with the extended family.
waysIn.action: Ask what made the visit feel especially easy.

templates.title: cousins reunited, chaos ensued
templates.description: A big extended family gathering turned into one of those chaotic-but-fun events that left everyone buzzing long after it wrapped up.

waysIn.title: Relive the chaos with them
waysIn.description: These big chaotic family moments become the stories people retell for years, let them tell it again and enjoy it just as much the second time.
waysIn.action: Ask for their favorite moment from the whole gathering.

templates.title: official family approval arc
templates.description: Someone from their partner's family said or did something that made them feel truly accepted into the fold, not just tolerated.

waysIn.title: Don't rush past the moment
waysIn.description: Feeling truly accepted by someone's family is a big deal, give it space instead of brushing it off as no big thing.
waysIn.action: Tell them you noticed how the family embraced them.

templates.title: aunt energy, immaculate
templates.description: An extended family member showed up for them in a way they didn't expect, and it left a genuinely good impression.

waysIn.title: Give credit where it's due
waysIn.description: When extended family shows up in a real way, it's worth acknowledging, it says something good about the family they're building around themselves.
waysIn.action: Mention it to them specifically, name the person and what they did.

templates.title: in-law energy: tense
templates.description: Something about interacting with their partner's family left them feeling on edge, like they can't fully be themselves around them.

waysIn.title: Stay neutral, not silent
waysIn.description: This isn't the moment to pick sides or defend anyone, just make sure they know you're not adding to the pressure.
waysIn.action: Ask them directly how they're feeling about it, away from the extended family.

templates.title: extended family, extended opinions
templates.description: They picked up on some judgment or unsolicited opinions from extended family, and it's left them feeling more self-conscious than usual.

waysIn.title: Reflect back what's true
waysIn.description: Outside opinions can chip away at confidence fast, remind them of who they actually are instead of letting the judgment sit unanswered.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what you admire about how they handled it.

templates.title: family drama, wrong side of it
templates.description: Some drama between extended family members ended up pulling them in, and now they're stuck navigating a conflict that isn't even theirs.

waysIn.title: Give them permission to opt out
waysIn.description: They don't have to solve someone else's family drama, remind them it's okay to stay neutral and protect their own peace.
waysIn.action: Help them come up with an exit line for the next time this drama comes up.

templates.title: extended family, extended energy drain
templates.description: A string of extended family obligations has left them running on empty, more performing "fine" than actually feeling it.

waysIn.title: Guard their downtime
waysIn.description: They've been giving a lot of energy to extended family, make sure there's real recovery time built in before the next ask comes.
waysIn.action: Block off some just-the-two-of-you time with zero family involved.

templates.title: roommate goals, actually
templates.description: Things at home with their roommate have been genuinely easy lately, good energy, no friction, the kind of living situation that just works.

waysIn.title: Notice the good setup
waysIn.description: A calm living situation is easy to take for granted, point out that it's not a given and they've built something good there.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been making the household dynamic feel so easy.

templates.title: roommate to friend arc
templates.description: They had a moment with their roommate that turned a functional living arrangement into an actual friendship, and it clearly made their day better.

waysIn.title: Root for the new dynamic
waysIn.description: A roommate becoming a real friend is a nice surprise, be genuinely happy about it instead of feeling like it's competing with your bond.
waysIn.action: Ask how the friendship with their roommate has been evolving.

templates.subScenario: Roommate Support in a Tough Moment
templates.title: roommate stepped up
templates.description: Their roommate showed up for them during a rough moment in a way they didn't expect, and it left a genuinely good impression.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge who helped
waysIn.description: It's a good thing they have someone at home who has their back too, credit that instead of feeling like it should've been you.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's great their roommate came through like that.

templates.title: roommate tension: rising
templates.description: Something's been off with their roommate lately, unspoken tension or an actual disagreement that's making home feel less relaxing than it should.

waysIn.title: Be the calm part of home
waysIn.description: If home doesn't feel peaceful, being with you should, don't add pressure by asking them to resolve it immediately.
waysIn.action: Ask if they want to vent about it or just want a distraction from it.

templates.title: dish duty diplomacy failed
templates.description: An ongoing disagreement about chores or fairness at home has been quietly grinding on them more than they're letting on.

waysIn.title: Don't minimize the small stuff
waysIn.description: Chore disputes sound petty from the outside but wear people down for real, take it seriously instead of brushing it off as trivial.
waysIn.action: Ask what a fair resolution would actually look like to them.

templates.title: living situation: a lot
templates.description: Something about their current living setup, noise, space, or just too many people, has been draining them more than usual.

waysIn.title: Give them somewhere else to breathe
waysIn.description: They don't need a plan to fix their living situation, they need a break from it, even a small one.
waysIn.action: Invite them somewhere outside the house just to get a change of scenery.

templates.title: roommate roulette incoming
templates.description: A roommate situation is changing, someone moving out or a new person moving in, and the uncertainty of it is unsettling them more than they're admitting.

waysIn.title: Be the constant during the change
waysIn.description: Living situations in flux are stressful in a low-grade, constant way, being a stable presence matters more than solving the logistics for them.
waysIn.action: Check in specifically about how they're feeling about the change, not just the practical details.

templates.title: certified W, publicly
templates.description: They got recognized out loud, in front of other people, for something they worked hard on, and that kind of visible credit hits differently.

waysIn.title: Make sure they know you noticed too
waysIn.description: Public praise feels good but private acknowledgment from you makes it land even deeper, don't assume the crowd's applause was enough.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what you think earned them that recognition.

templates.title: compliment landed different
templates.description: Someone said something kind and genuine to them out of nowhere, and it clearly stuck with them longer than a passing compliment usually does.

waysIn.title: Repeat the good thing
waysIn.description: A compliment sticks harder when more than one person says it, echo whatever landed so well instead of assuming it's already sunk in.
waysIn.action: Tell them you agree with whatever the compliment was about.

templates.subScenario: Recognized For Effort, Not Just Results
templates.title: the grind got noticed
templates.description: Someone acknowledged the actual effort behind what they've been doing, not just the outcome, and being seen for the work itself meant a lot.

waysIn.title: Notice the work, not just the win
waysIn.description: They've probably been putting in effort you haven't fully clocked, name the process itself, not just whatever the result was.
waysIn.action: Bring up something specific about their effort that you've actually noticed.

templates.title: main character on the internet
templates.description: Something they posted or did got a wave of unexpected attention online, and the novelty of that kind of visibility has them a little buzzed.

waysIn.title: Be hyped, not weird about it
waysIn.description: This is a fun, low-stakes moment, match their excitement instead of downplaying the internet attention as silly or unserious.
waysIn.action: Screenshot your favorite comment or reaction and send it to them.

templates.title: credit went missing
templates.description: They put in real work on something and didn't get the credit or acknowledgment they were expecting, and it's bothering them more than they're saying.

waysIn.title: Say what should've been said
waysIn.description: They didn't get the recognition they deserved from whoever should've given it, you can still be the one who says it plainly.
waysIn.action: Tell them directly what they should've been credited for.

templates.title: main character, wrong scene
templates.description: Something a little embarrassing happened to them in front of other people, and even if they're laughing it off, it's still sitting with them.

waysIn.title: Make it feel small again
waysIn.description: The fastest way to shrink an embarrassing moment is shared laughter, not reassurance, join them in finding it funny instead of being overly comforting.
waysIn.action: Bring it up lightly and laugh about it together, let them lead the tone.

templates.title: internet said something mean
templates.description: They got some unexpectedly harsh feedback or comments online, and it's clearly gotten under their skin more than they'd like to admit.

waysIn.title: Be the louder, kinder voice
waysIn.description: A few negative comments can outweigh a hundred good ones in someone's head, counter that with something specific and genuine.
waysIn.action: Tell them one specific thing you think they got right that the comments missed.

templates.title: did the thing, no one clocked it
templates.description: They did something they were proud of and it just... passed without anyone really noticing, and that quiet letdown is more real than they're letting on.

waysIn.title: Point out what everyone else missed
waysIn.description: This is a low moment to just be the one person who actually saw it, don't wait for a bigger reason to bring it up.
waysIn.action: Bring it up unprompted and tell them exactly what you noticed.

templates.title: terminally online, but make it wholesome
templates.description: They had a genuinely good exchange online, a comment thread, a DM conversation, something that reminded them the internet can be a good place too.

waysIn.title: Get curious about their internet win
waysIn.description: Online moments feel less real to outsiders but they're real to the person living them, take it as seriously as any in-person good moment.
waysIn.action: Ask them to show you the thing that made their day online.

templates.title: the algorithm chose correctly
templates.description: Something they made or shared online got a genuinely good response, and seeing people connect with their creative side clearly gave them a boost.

waysIn.title: Engage like it matters, because it does
waysIn.description: A like from you means more than a hundred strangers, treat their creative online moment like the win it actually is.
waysIn.action: Tell them your honest favorite part of what they posted.

templates.title: internet strangers, now besties
templates.description: They found a corner of the internet, a group, a community, that actually gets them, and it's clearly given them a sense of belonging.

waysIn.title: Be glad they found their people
waysIn.description: Online communities are a real form of belonging, treat it that way instead of treating it as less legitimate than in-person friendships.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been the best part of finding that space.

templates.title: caught up in the discourse
templates.description: They got pulled into some back-and-forth online, comments, a group chat, a thread, and it's left them more rattled than the situation probably deserves.

waysIn.title: Make it easy to log off
waysIn.description: Online conflict is easy to spiral in, help them step away from the screen instead of rehashing every reply with them.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing something completely offline together to reset.

templates.title: everyone's highlight reel, one feed
templates.description: Scrolling has left them feeling a little behind or not-enough compared to everyone else's curated version of their life.

waysIn.title: Remind them of the highlight-reel effect
waysIn.description: Comparison spirals feed on incomplete pictures, gently point out the gap between someone's feed and their actual life without dismissing the feeling.
waysIn.action: Point out something real and good in their actual life, specifically.

templates.title: internet has entered the chat
templates.description: They got called out or criticized online in a way that felt more personal than they expected, and it's clearly shaken their confidence a bit.

waysIn.title: Remind them who they actually are
waysIn.description: A callout can make someone feel reduced to one moment, remind them of the fuller picture of who they are outside of it.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that this doesn't change how you see them.

templates.title: terminally online, tired version
templates.description: They've been deep in a scrolling spiral, more numb than entertained by it, and it's clearly left them a little foggy and low-energy.

waysIn.title: Give them a reason to put the phone down
waysIn.description: They probably know the scrolling isn't helping, a genuinely appealing alternative works better than pointing out the obvious.
waysIn.action: Suggest something fun to do together that has nothing to do with a screen.

templates.title: bag secured
templates.description: They got officially recognized at work, a promotion, a raise, a title bump, and it's the kind of validation that quietly changes how they carry themselves.

waysIn.title: Don't let it pass quietly
waysIn.description: This deserves more than a "congrats" text, treat it like the milestone it is, not just another Tuesday update.
waysIn.action: Plan something to actually mark the moment, even something small.

templates.title: shipped it, and it worked
templates.description: Something they'd been grinding on for a while finally came together, and the relief of it actually working out is written all over them.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge what it took
waysIn.description: The outcome is the visible part, but the effort behind it is what actually deserves the credit, name that specifically.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of the process they're proudest of.

templates.title: new job, who dis
templates.description: They landed a new role or made a career move they'd been wanting, and there's a fresh kind of excitement in how they're talking about work now.

waysIn.title: Get into the new-job energy with them
waysIn.description: New job excitement is contagious for a reason, lean into it with them instead of jumping straight to logistics or advice.
waysIn.action: Ask what they're most looking forward to in the new role.

templates.title: manager era: impressed
templates.description: Someone above them at work specifically called out their work in a way that felt genuine, and that kind of recognition clearly landed.

waysIn.title: Add your own to theirs
waysIn.description: Recognition from a boss is validating, but recognition from you is personal, don't assume the professional praise covers it.
waysIn.action: Tell them exactly what you think they did well, in your own words.

templates.title: quit and never looked back
templates.description: They made the call to leave a job that wasn't serving them anymore, and there's real pride sitting underneath the relief of finally choosing themselves.

waysIn.title: Reinforce the courage
waysIn.description: Walking away from something stable takes real nerve, make sure they know you're solidly behind the decision instead of quietly questioning it.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically why you think it was the right call.

templates.title: career plot twist, unwanted
templates.description: They lost their job unexpectedly, and underneath however they're handling it on the surface, there's real uncertainty sitting with them.

waysIn.title: Be the certainty
waysIn.description: Everything about their next steps is suddenly uncertain, don't add to that by rushing toward solutions, just be a stable, unpanicked presence.
waysIn.action: Ask what would actually feel helpful, logistics talk or a total distraction.

templates.title: almost, but not quite
templates.description: They didn't get the promotion, role, or opportunity they were hoping for, and the disappointment is bigger than they're letting show.

waysIn.title: Let it be disappointing
waysIn.description: This doesn't need to be reframed into a lesson right away, let them sit in the letdown before jumping to silver linings.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that their disappointment makes total sense.

templates.title: workplace drama, unwanted subscription
templates.description: Some tension with a coworker or manager has been following them home from work, more than a one-off bad day.

waysIn.title: Don't let work follow them here
waysIn.description: They're probably replaying the situation enough at work, give them a genuine break from it instead of dissecting it further.
waysIn.action: Suggest something completely unrelated to work to shift the focus for a bit.

templates.title: burnout arc, in progress
templates.description: Work has been draining them for a stretch now, and the exhaustion has stopped being occasional and started being their baseline.

waysIn.title: Make rest non-negotiable
waysIn.description: They probably feel like they can't fully stop, help make actual rest feel allowed instead of one more thing to feel behind on.
waysIn.action: Take something off their plate, even something small and unrelated to work.

templates.title: interview: crushed
templates.description: An interview they were nervous about actually went really well, and the confidence boost from that is still visible in how they're carrying themselves.

waysIn.title: Let them stay in the high
waysIn.description: Post-good-interview confidence is fragile and worth protecting, don't rush to "what if it doesn't work out," just let them enjoy having nailed it.
waysIn.action: Ask what moment in the interview felt the strongest.

templates.title: they want them, obviously
templates.description: They got an offer they were hoping for, and there's real relief mixed in with the excitement after however long the search has been going.

waysIn.title: Mark the end of the search
waysIn.description: A job search takes a real toll even when it ends well, celebrate that the whole process is finally over, not just the offer itself.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels to finally be done with the search.

templates.title: job hunt, but make it hopeful
templates.description: After a stretch of a tough search, something shifted, a good lead, a good conversation, and their energy around the job hunt is noticeably more hopeful.

waysIn.title: Match their renewed hope
waysIn.description: This is a fragile but good shift in energy, reinforce it with genuine optimism instead of hedging with caution about the process.
waysIn.action: Ask what's got them feeling more hopeful about it.

templates.title: so close, then nothing
templates.description: They didn't get a role they interviewed for and felt genuinely good about, and that specific kind of near-miss disappointment is harder to shake.

waysIn.title: Don't rush to the next step
waysIn.description: This one stings more because it felt so close, let them feel that fully before pivoting to "on to the next one" energy.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that the rejection doesn't reflect how they actually did.

templates.title: job hunt: extended edition
templates.description: The job search has been dragging on longer than they expected, and the fatigue of it is starting to wear on their confidence, not just their patience.

waysIn.title: Remind them of their worth outside the search
waysIn.description: A long search can make someone feel defined by rejection, remind them of their value in a way that has nothing to do with job hunting.
waysIn.action: Tell them something you admire about them that has nothing to do with work.

templates.title: nerves: fully activated
templates.description: An upcoming interview has them spiraling a little more than usual, overthinking every possible question and outcome.

waysIn.title: Bring them back to the present
waysIn.description: They don't need more prep advice, they need to come down from the spiral, help ground them instead of adding more to think about.
waysIn.action: Do something calming together right before the interview, nothing related to prepping further.

templates.title: radio silence, professionally
templates.description: An employer went quiet after seeming interested, no rejection, no update, just silence, and the not-knowing is more frustrating than a clear no would be.

waysIn.title: Validate the specific annoyance
waysIn.description: Being ghosted professionally has a unique kind of frustration to it, name that specifically instead of generic reassurance about the search.
waysIn.action: Let them vent about how unprofessional the silence feels, no need to problem-solve it.

templates.title: the team actually teamed
templates.description: Something clicked with their team or coworkers this stretch, a project that flowed well, real collaboration, and it left them genuinely energized by work.

waysIn.title: Let the good work-mood carry over
waysIn.description: Good team energy is a nice, lighter kind of work high, meet it with genuine interest instead of treating work talk as an obligation to sit through.
waysIn.action: Ask what made the team dynamic click.

templates.title: work bestie unlocked
templates.description: They've connected with a coworker who actually gets it, someone who makes the day-to-day at work noticeably better just by being there.

waysIn.title: Root for their work friendship
waysIn.description: Having a real ally at work changes everything about how a job feels, be genuinely happy they've found that instead of feeling replaced.
waysIn.action: Ask what it is about that coworker that makes work better.

templates.title: taught someone something
templates.description: They stepped into a mentoring or guiding role for someone at work, and there's a quiet pride in having helped someone else figure something out.

waysIn.title: Point out what that says about them
waysIn.description: Being sought out to mentor or guide someone says something real about how they're seen, name that instead of letting it go unspoken.
waysIn.action: Tell them what kind of person it takes to be the one others go to for help.

templates.title: cubicle beef
templates.description: Tension with a specific coworker has been building, and it's turning into the kind of low-grade stress that follows them out of the office.

waysIn.title: Let them just get it out
waysIn.description: They probably don't need a strategy for handling the coworker, they need somewhere to unload it without it turning into a planning session.
waysIn.action: Let them fully vent about it without jumping to "have you tried..." advice.

templates.title: boss battle, unwinnable
templates.description: Their manager has been a consistent source of stress lately, unclear expectations, unfair pressure, or just a mismatch in how they work.

waysIn.title: Reflect reality back to them
waysIn.description: A difficult manager can make someone start doubting their own competence, remind them what's actually true about their work.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what you know they're good at, to counter the self-doubt.

templates.title: not in that group chat
templates.description: They've noticed they're a bit on the outside of the social dynamics at work, left out of plans or inside jokes in a way that's landed harder than expected.

waysIn.title: Be the place they feel fully included
waysIn.description: Feeling like an outsider anywhere is isolating, make sure at least one part of their life feels like full, easy belonging.
waysIn.action: Plan something that makes them feel fully chosen and included, no work context involved.

templates.title: doing the work, missing the thanks
templates.description: They've been putting in real effort at work without it being acknowledged, and the lack of recognition is starting to wear on their motivation.

waysIn.title: Be the appreciation they're missing
waysIn.description: If work isn't giving them the credit they've earned, don't wait for that to change before you give it yourself.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what you see them doing well that's going unnoticed.

templates.title: exam: defeated
templates.description: They got through a major exam or test they'd been stressing over, and the relief of it being done and going well is written all over them.

waysIn.title: Give the relief room to breathe
waysIn.description: The stress before an exam is intense, so is the relief after, let them fully enjoy that it's over instead of immediately asking what's next.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels now that it's actually done.

templates.title: officially done, officially proud
templates.description: They finished a program, degree, or course they'd put real time into, and there's a quiet sense of accomplishment sitting underneath the relief.

waysIn.title: Treat the ending like the milestone it is
waysIn.description: Finishing something long-term deserves real acknowledgment, not a passing mention, make sure it feels marked, not just noted.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of the whole journey they're proudest of.

templates.title: credentials: secured
templates.description: They completed a certification they'd been working toward, and it's giving them a concrete sense of progress they can point to.

waysIn.title: Treat the proof like it matters
waysIn.description: A certification is proof of effort they can hold onto, reinforce that it's a real accomplishment, not just paperwork.
waysIn.action: Ask what doors this opens up for them next.

templates.title: exam: didn't go their way
templates.description: An exam or test didn't go how they hoped, and the disappointment is sitting heavier than they're showing on the surface.

waysIn.title: Remind them this isn't a verdict on them
waysIn.description: One result can feel like it says something bigger about them, gently push back on that instead of letting the disappointment generalize.
waysIn.action: Remind them of a time they bounced back from something similar.

templates.title: syllabus week never ended
templates.description: Coursework or academic responsibilities have been piling up, and they're running on stress and deadlines more than actual bandwidth.

waysIn.title: Lighten a non-academic load
waysIn.description: You can't do their assignments for them, but you can make everything else easier, take something small off their plate outside of school.
waysIn.action: Handle something unrelated to their coursework so they have one less thing to think about.

templates.title: wondering if this is worth it
templates.description: They've been quietly questioning whether to keep going with a program or path they're on, more doubt than certainty.

waysIn.title: Let them think out loud without pressure
waysIn.description: This isn't the moment to talk them out of quitting or push them to stay the course, just let them process the uncertainty without steering it.
waysIn.action: Ask what's actually behind the doubt, and just listen.

templates.title: skill unlocked, no cap
templates.description: Something they've been practicing finally clicked, and that specific feeling of a skill "clicking" has them noticeably lit up.

waysIn.title: Ask to see it in action
waysIn.description: Skills feel more real once someone else sees them, ask to actually witness it instead of just hearing about it secondhand.
waysIn.action: Ask them to show you the thing they just figured out.

templates.title: the grind is showing
templates.description: Time and consistency spent on a skill is starting to visibly pay off, and they're noticing their own progress in a way that's genuinely motivating.

waysIn.title: Point out how far they've come
waysIn.description: They're probably too close to their own progress to see it clearly, name specifically what's improved since they started.
waysIn.action: Tell them one specific thing that's noticeably better than when they started.

templates.subScenario: Took On a New Skill / Challenge
templates.title: beginner mode, activated
templates.description: They started learning something completely new, and there's an excited, slightly nervous energy that comes with being a total beginner again.

waysIn.title: Make starting feel exciting, not scary
waysIn.description: Starting something new as an adult takes a specific kind of courage, treat their beginner status as exciting rather than something to be self-conscious about.
waysIn.action: Ask what made them want to pick this particular thing up.

templates.title: stuck on the same level
templates.description: They've hit a plateau with something they're learning, and the lack of visible progress is testing their patience more than the skill itself is.

waysIn.title: Remind them plateaus are part of it
waysIn.description: Plateaus feel like failure but they're actually just part of learning anything, reframe it that way instead of letting the frustration turn into self-doubt.
waysIn.action: Remind them that the plateau doesn't cancel out the progress that came before it.

templates.title: motivation: running low
templates.description: Their motivation to keep learning something is fading, and they're quietly weighing whether it's even worth continuing.

waysIn.title: Let it be their call, fully
waysIn.description: This isn't the moment to convince them to push through or to bail, just let them know either choice is fine with you.
waysIn.action: Ask what originally made them want to start, without steering toward an answer.

templates.subScenario: Embarrassed By a Mistake While Learning
templates.title: rookie mistake, publicly made
templates.description: They made a visible mistake while still learning something, and the embarrassment of it is bigger in their head than it probably was to anyone watching.

waysIn.title: Make the mistake feel normal
waysIn.description: Beginner mistakes feel huge in the moment but they're just part of the process, treat it lightly instead of over-comforting them about it.
waysIn.action: Tell them about a time you messed up learning something, to make it feel shared.

templates.title: PR unlocked
templates.description: They hit a fitness goal they'd been working toward, and the sense of physical accomplishment has them walking a little taller.

waysIn.title: Celebrate the milestone, not just the number
waysIn.description: This is a genuine achievement, treat it like one instead of a passing "nice," specific hype lands better than generic praise here.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of hitting the goal felt the best.

templates.title: showing up, no days off
templates.description: They've kept up a real streak of consistency with working out or moving their body, and the discipline of it is clearly boosting their mood overall.

waysIn.title: Name the consistency, not just results
waysIn.description: Showing up consistently is harder than any single workout, acknowledge the discipline itself rather than waiting for a visible before-and-after.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed how consistent they've been.

templates.title: tried a new sport, survived
templates.description: They tried a new physical activity or sport for the first time, and there's a fun, slightly proud energy about stepping outside their usual routine.

waysIn.title: Match the new-activity energy
waysIn.description: Trying something new physically takes a little nerve, meet that with genuine curiosity instead of just a quick "cool."
waysIn.action: Ask what surprised them most about trying it.

templates.title: benched, unwillingly
templates.description: An injury or setback has knocked them out of their usual physical routine, and the frustration of being sidelined is bigger than the injury itself.

waysIn.title: Don't rush to silver linings
waysIn.description: Being sidelined from something they care about is genuinely frustrating, sit with that instead of immediately offering workarounds or bright sides.
waysIn.action: Ask what they miss most about their usual routine.

templates.title: gym motivation: on vacation
templates.description: Their motivation to work out or move has quietly faded, and the gap between where they were and where they are now is nagging at them.

waysIn.title: Take the pressure off first
waysIn.description: Guilt about lost momentum makes it harder to restart, not easier, take the pressure off before anyone talks about getting back on track.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing something active together, low-stakes, no goal attached.

templates.title: not feeling it in their body
templates.description: They've been feeling off or frustrated in their own body lately, more of a general discomfort than tied to any one specific event.

waysIn.title: Speak to how they feel, not how they look
waysIn.description: Compliments about appearance can miss the mark here, focus on affirming who they are and how capable they are instead of commenting on looks.
waysIn.action: Plan something that makes them feel good and capable in their body, not focused on appearance.

templates.title: body gave the green light
templates.description: They got a good result from a checkup or test they'd been a little worried about, and the relief of good news is visibly lifting their mood.

waysIn.title: Celebrate the relief itself
waysIn.description: Good health news deserves its own moment of relief, don't rush past it to "back to normal," let them actually feel the weight lift.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels now that the worry is off their plate.

templates.title: officially un-sick
templates.description: They're finally feeling like themselves again after being unwell for a stretch, and there's real relief in getting their energy back.

waysIn.title: Make their return feel good
waysIn.description: Getting back to normal after being unwell deserves a little celebration, not a return to business as usual with no acknowledgment.
waysIn.action: Do something that marks feeling better, nothing elaborate, just intentional.

templates.subScenario: Positive Change in a Health Habit
templates.title: new habit, sticking
templates.description: A health-related change they've been trying to make is actually sticking, and they're noticing the difference it's making in how they feel.

waysIn.title: Notice the difference out loud
waysIn.description: Habit changes are easy to take for granted once they become routine, point out what's improved so it doesn't go unnoticed.
waysIn.action: Tell them something specific you've noticed feels different about them lately.

templates.title: body said no
templates.description: They haven't been feeling well physically, and pushing through it is clearly taking more out of them than they're letting on.

waysIn.title: Remove the guilt from resting
waysIn.description: They probably feel like they should be pushing through, make it easy for them to just rest instead of feeling like they're falling behind.
waysIn.action: Take something small off their plate so they can actually rest.

templates.title: body took an L
templates.description: They got hurt or injured, and beyond the physical discomfort, the disruption to their normal routine is frustrating them too.

waysIn.title: Help with the practical stuff
waysIn.description: An injury messes with someone's independence in small, annoying ways, offering practical help matters more than sympathy.
waysIn.action: Ask what's become harder to do and offer to help with that specific thing.

templates.title: waiting on an answer
templates.description: They got a concerning result or are waiting to hear back about something health-related, and the uncertainty is clearly weighing on them more than they're voicing.

waysIn.title: Don't rush to reassure
waysIn.description: This isn't a moment for confident reassurance you can't actually promise, just be steady and present while they wait, without minimizing the worry.
waysIn.action: Check in without pushing for updates, and let them lead on what they want to share.

templates.title: running on fumes, physically
templates.description: They're physically worn down, more tired than a good night's sleep can fix, and it's starting to show in their mood and energy overall.

waysIn.title: Guard their recovery time
waysIn.description: They probably won't ask for the break they need, protect their downtime proactively instead of waiting for them to request it.
waysIn.action: Clear something off their schedule so they have real, uninterrupted time to rest.

templates.title: slept like it was a job
templates.description: They've been sleeping genuinely well for a stretch, and the difference in their mood and focus from actually resting is pretty noticeable.

waysIn.title: Help them keep the streak going
waysIn.description: A good sleep streak is fragile and worth protecting, avoid making plans that would mess with the routine that's clearly working for them.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been different about their routine that's making the sleep so good.

templates.title: sleep schedule: repaired
templates.description: They pulled their sleep schedule back on track after a rough stretch of bad hours, and there's real satisfaction in feeling more regulated again.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge the effort it took
waysIn.description: Resetting a sleep schedule takes actual discipline, treat it as the accomplishment it is instead of assuming it just happened on its own.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed they seem more like themselves lately.

templates.title: brain won't log off
templates.description: They've been struggling to actually fall or stay asleep, and the exhaustion from it is starting to affect more than just their energy.

waysIn.title: Help create an off-ramp for their brain
waysIn.description: They probably can't just decide to sleep better, help create conditions that make winding down easier instead of just telling them to rest.
waysIn.action: Suggest a calm, screen-free activity together before bed.

templates.title: sleep schedule in shambles
templates.description: Their sleep schedule has gotten completely irregular, odd hours, inconsistent nights, and the disorientation of it is starting to affect their mood.

waysIn.title: Give their day one steady point
waysIn.description: A chaotic schedule feels less overwhelming with at least one fixed, reliable point in the day, be that anchor rather than adding more variables.
waysIn.action: Set one small, consistent plan together that gives their day some structure.

templates.title: low battery, no charger in sight
templates.description: They've been low on energy for a stretch, not tied to any one clear cause, just a general depletion that's affecting how present they feel.

waysIn.title: Make low-energy time still count
waysIn.description: They don't need a big plan, they need permission to do less, make low-key time together feel like enough.
waysIn.action: Suggest the lowest-effort version of hanging out, no pressure to do more than that.

templates.title: money fell from the sky
templates.description: Unexpected money came their way, a bonus, a gift, a refund, and the little jolt of good luck has them in a noticeably lighter mood.

waysIn.title: Match the good-luck energy
waysIn.description: Unexpected money is just fun, no need to talk strategy or savings right away, let them enjoy the small win first.
waysIn.action: Ask what they're most tempted to do with it.

templates.subScenario: Paid Off Debt / Financial Weight Lifted
templates.title: financial weight: lifted
templates.description: They paid off something they'd been carrying for a while, and the relief of that specific weight being gone is bigger than the number itself.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge what it took to get there
waysIn.description: Paying something off takes real discipline over time, name that effort directly instead of treating it as just a number going to zero.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels to have that weight off their shoulders.

templates.title: financial glow-up moment
templates.description: A financial decision they made is clearly paying off now, and there's a quiet confidence in having made the right call.

waysIn.title: Point out the good judgment behind it
waysIn.description: This is a good moment to reflect their competence back to them, name the decision-making itself, not just the result.
waysIn.action: Tell them that decision was smarter than they're giving themselves credit for.

templates.title: budget, ambushed
templates.description: An unexpected expense threw off their plans, and the frustration of it is less about the money and more about feeling caught off guard.

waysIn.title: Don't turn it into a budgeting talk
waysIn.description: They don't need advice on planning for the unexpected, they need the frustration acknowledged without a follow-up lesson.
waysIn.action: Let them vent about the timing of it without offering a fix.

templates.title: budget on struggle mode
templates.description: Money's been tight for them lately, and the low-grade stress of watching every dollar is wearing on them more than they're saying.

waysIn.title: Make quality time free
waysIn.description: This isn't the moment to suggest anything expensive, however casually, plan something that costs nothing and still feels special.
waysIn.action: Plan a genuinely free activity that still feels like real, intentional time together.

templates.title: spent it, regretted it
templates.description: They're second-guessing a financial decision they made, and the regret is nagging at them more than the actual dollar amount probably warrants.

waysIn.title: Don't pile on the regret
waysIn.description: They're already being hard enough on themselves about it, resist adding any commentary about what they should've done instead.
waysIn.action: Tell them everyone's made a purchase they regretted, and move on lightly.

templates.title: manifested, then bought
templates.description: They finally got something they've wanted for a while, and there's a genuine little thrill in finally having it after all the waiting or saving.

waysIn.title: Be excited without judgment
waysIn.description: This is a pure, uncomplicated good mood, match it without adding any commentary about cost or practicality.
waysIn.action: Ask to see it or hear all about it, full enthusiasm.

templates.title: main character upgrade
templates.description: They upgraded something that actually improves their day-to-day, and the improvement is genuinely making life easier.

waysIn.title: Point out how it's already helping
waysIn.description: Practical upgrades feel less exciting than fun purchases but still deserve acknowledgment, notice the real difference it's making.
waysIn.action: Ask how it's already made things easier since they got it.

templates.title: someone gets them
templates.description: They received a gift that actually felt thoughtful and personal, and being truly seen through a gift clearly meant more than the item itself.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge the thoughtfulness, not just the item
waysIn.description: What made this land wasn't the object, it was feeling understood, reflect that back instead of just commenting on the gift itself.
waysIn.action: Ask what made the gift feel so spot-on to them.

templates.title: gone too soon
templates.description: Something they cared about got lost or broken, and the frustration of it is sitting heavier than the item's actual value might suggest.

waysIn.title: Don't minimize the loss
waysIn.description: Even small losses can feel disproportionately frustrating, let it be annoying without immediately offering a replacement or a bright side.
waysIn.action: Let them vent about it fully before moving on to anything practical.

templates.subScenario: Buyer's Guilt Over a Big Purchase
templates.title: treated themself, now spiraling
templates.description: They made a bigger purchase and are now second-guessing whether it was worth it, more guilt than enjoyment of the thing itself.

waysIn.title: Take the guilt off the table
waysIn.description: They probably need permission to just enjoy what they bought, reassure them it's fine instead of weighing in on whether it was worth it.
waysIn.action: Point out one genuine reason the purchase was a good call.

templates.title: plot twist: it's broken
templates.description: Something they rely on stopped working unexpectedly, and beyond the hassle of fixing it, the timing of it is adding real stress.

waysIn.title: Take a task, not just offer sympathy
waysIn.description: This is a practical problem more than an emotional one, offering to help handle a piece of the logistics matters more than sympathy alone.
waysIn.action: Offer to take on one concrete task related to fixing or replacing it.

templates.title: savings goal: secured
templates.description: They hit a savings goal they'd been working toward, and there's real satisfaction in seeing that discipline actually pay off.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge the delayed gratification
waysIn.description: Saving up for something takes real patience, name that specifically instead of only celebrating once the goal is spent.
waysIn.action: Ask what they're most excited to do now that the goal is met.

templates.title: saving money, unbothered
templates.description: They've built a more consistent savings habit, and the sense of control that comes with it is clearly boosting their confidence.

waysIn.title: Name the security it's building
waysIn.description: This is about more than money, it's about feeling more in control, reflect that back instead of just commenting on the numbers.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed they seem less stressed about money lately.

templates.title: savings goal: reset
templates.description: Something set their savings progress back, and the frustration of losing ground after real effort is bigger than the setback itself.

waysIn.title: Remind them the effort still counted
waysIn.description: A setback can make someone feel like the whole effort was pointless, remind them that isn't true, the progress still happened.
waysIn.action: Remind them they've done it before and can rebuild it again.

templates.title: saving money, hard mode
templates.description: They've been trying to save consistently and it's not sticking, and the frustration of feeling stuck is wearing on their confidence.

waysIn.title: Take the shame out of it
waysIn.description: Struggling to save doesn't say anything bad about them, remove any implied judgment before offering any kind of encouragement.
waysIn.action: Remind them that consistency is hard for almost everyone, not just them.

templates.title: finally finished it
templates.description: They completed a creative project they'd been chipping away at, and finally finishing it has them buzzing with a mix of pride and relief.

waysIn.title: Treat the finished thing like it matters
waysIn.description: Finishing a personal project deserves genuine attention, not a quick glance, actually engage with what they made.
waysIn.action: Ask to properly see or experience the finished project, not just hear about it.

templates.title: the passion project popped off
templates.description: Something they made got a genuinely good response from other people, and having their creative side recognized clearly means a lot to them.

waysIn.title: Be another real fan
waysIn.description: Outside recognition feels good, but your genuine reaction still carries its own weight, don't assume the other praise already covers it.
waysIn.action: Tell them your specific honest opinion of what they made.

templates.subScenario: Found Renewed Passion for a Project
templates.title: passion project, back online
templates.description: Their motivation for a project they'd let sit for a while has come back, and there's real excitement in returning to something that matters to them.

waysIn.title: Show interest before it fades again
waysIn.description: Renewed motivation can be fragile, show genuine curiosity now while the excitement is fresh instead of waiting to see if it sticks.
waysIn.action: Ask what got them excited about it again.

templates.title: put it out there, crickets
templates.description: They put something they made out into the world and it didn't get the response they hoped for, and the quiet disappointment of that is real.

waysIn.title: Give it the attention it deserves
waysIn.description: The outside response may have fallen flat, but your genuine engagement can still make it feel worth having made, give it real attention.
waysIn.action: Ask to see the project and tell them specifically what you like about it.

templates.title: creative block, fully loading
templates.description: They've hit a wall with a project they care about, and the frustration of not being able to move it forward is wearing on them.

waysIn.title: Remove the deadline energy
waysIn.description: Creative blocks usually get worse under pressure, take away any implied urgency instead of asking when it'll be finished.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing something completely unrelated to reset their head for a bit.

templates.title: passion project, on pause
templates.description: They've quietly stepped away from a project they used to be excited about, and there's a mix of relief and guilt in having let it go.

waysIn.title: Let it be okay to walk away
waysIn.description: Not every project needs to be finished, help them feel okay about stepping back instead of encouraging them to push through out of obligation.
waysIn.action: Remind them that starting it wasn't a waste, even if it ends here.

templates.title: new hobby, full send
templates.description: They've thrown themselves into a new hobby with genuine enthusiasm, and that specific energy of a fresh interest is clearly lighting them up.

waysIn.title: Let them talk about it as much as they want
waysIn.description: New-hobby excitement wants an audience, let them go on about it without cutting it short, even if the details are lost on you.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of the new hobby they're most excited about.

templates.title: found their people, hobby edition
templates.description: A hobby has connected them with a new group of people who share the same interest, and that sense of belonging is clearly adding something good.

waysIn.title: Be glad they found their people
waysIn.description: Finding community through a shared interest is a real kind of belonging, treat it that way instead of feeling like it's separate from your world.
waysIn.action: Ask what the people in this new group are like.

templates.subScenario: Struggling to Get Into a New Hobby
templates.title: new hobby, harder than expected
templates.description: A new hobby is proving harder or less fun than they expected, and the gap between the excitement of starting and the reality now is discouraging them.

waysIn.title: Take the pressure off getting good at it
waysIn.description: They probably feel pressure to be good at it already, remind them the point was to enjoy it, not master it.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing it together in a low-pressure, just-for-fun way.

templates.subScenario: Hobby Feels Like a Chore Now
templates.title: hobby became a homework assignment
templates.description: Something that used to feel fun has started to feel like an obligation instead, and the shift from enjoyment to pressure is draining the appeal.

waysIn.title: Remind them it's supposed to be fun
waysIn.description: A hobby that stops being fun doesn't have to be forced, remind them there's no rule that says they have to keep going.
waysIn.action: Ask if they still actually want to do it, or if it's time to let it go.

templates.title: unlocked a new favorite place
templates.description: A trip they took turned out even better than expected, and they're still riding the high of how good it felt to be somewhere new.

waysIn.title: Ask for the full recap
waysIn.description: Good trips deserve a proper debrief, not a one-line summary, ask enough questions that they get to relive it a little.
waysIn.action: Ask for their single favorite moment from the whole trip.

templates.title: did it alone, thrived
templates.description: They took on a trip by themselves and came back with a noticeable boost in confidence from having navigated it solo.

waysIn.title: Admire the confidence, not just the trip
waysIn.description: Solo travel builds a specific kind of self-trust, name that directly instead of only talking about the places they saw.
waysIn.action: Ask what they learned about themselves from doing it alone.

templates.title: came back a little different
templates.description: Something about the trip gave them a genuine shift in perspective, and they're clearly still processing how much it affected them.

waysIn.title: Give the shift room to be real
waysIn.description: A perspective shift from travel can be hard to put into words right away, give them space to think out loud instead of asking for quick conclusions.
waysIn.action: Ask what surprised them most about how it changed their thinking.

templates.title: travel plans: derailed
templates.description: A trip didn't go according to plan, and the frustration of a disrupted trip is bigger than the logistics themselves might suggest.

waysIn.title: Help turn it into a good story
waysIn.description: Travel disasters often become the best stories eventually, help nudge it toward that framing once the initial frustration has had room to land.
waysIn.action: Ask what the most chaotic part of the whole thing was.

templates.title: travel anxiety, fully engaged
templates.description: An upcoming trip has them more anxious than excited, overthinking logistics or worst-case scenarios more than usual.

waysIn.title: Help simplify, not add more to think about
waysIn.description: They probably don't need more things to plan for, help simplify one specific worry instead of adding new contingencies.
waysIn.action: Ask what the single biggest worry is and help think through just that one thing.

templates.title: away and missing home
templates.description: They're away from home and it's hitting harder than expected, more homesickness than the excitement of being somewhere new.

waysIn.title: Make the distance feel smaller
waysIn.description: Being away is easier with a small tether to home, be that familiar presence rather than only encouraging them to make the most of the trip.
waysIn.action: Check in with something small and familiar that reminds them of home.

templates.title: zero plans, ten out of ten
templates.description: A last-minute, unplanned idea turned into a genuinely great time, and there's a specific kind of joy that comes from spontaneity actually working out.

waysIn.title: Give credit to their spontaneous side
waysIn.description: Spontaneous wins feel extra good because they weren't guaranteed, celebrate the instinct to just go for it, not just the outcome.
waysIn.action: Ask what made them decide to do it in the first place.

templates.subScenario: Stepped Out of Their Comfort Zone
templates.title: did the scary thing anyway
templates.description: They pushed past their usual comfort zone for something spontaneous, and the pride from that is more about the courage than the activity itself.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge what it took, not just what happened
waysIn.description: Stepping outside a comfort zone takes real nerve, name that specifically instead of just reacting to the fun story that came out of it.
waysIn.action: Tell them you're proud of them for doing something outside their comfort zone.

templates.title: winged it, regretted it
templates.description: An unplanned decision didn't go the way they hoped, and there's a mix of frustration and embarrassment about how it turned out.

waysIn.title: Praise the willingness to try
waysIn.description: The instinct to be spontaneous is still a good one even when the outcome wasn't, praise the willingness to try rather than the result.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of it, if any, was still worth it.

templates.title: should've said yes
templates.description: They passed on something spontaneous and are now second-guessing that decision, more regret than relief about playing it safe.

waysIn.title: Take the sting out of the what-if
waysIn.description: Dwelling on a missed opportunity rarely helps, gently redirect toward what's ahead instead of relitigating the decision.
waysIn.action: Suggest something spontaneous now as a way to move past it.

templates.title: plot development: exciting
templates.description: A big life change is underway, and instead of dread, they're actually feeling genuine excitement about what's ahead.

waysIn.title: Match their forward-looking energy
waysIn.description: This is a good moment to be genuinely hyped about the future with them, rather than focusing on the logistics of the change itself.
waysIn.action: Ask what they're most looking forward to about this next chapter.

templates.subScenario: Successfully Adjusted to a Big Change
templates.title: new normal, actually normal now
templates.description: A big change that used to feel disorienting finally feels settled, and there's real relief in things starting to feel normal again.

waysIn.title: Notice how far they've come
waysIn.description: Adjusting to change takes real time and effort that's easy to overlook once it's done, name that progress instead of treating it as no big deal.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed how much more settled they seem.

templates.title: made the leap
templates.description: They made a bold, deliberate choice to change something significant in their life, and there's real conviction behind the decision.

waysIn.title: Reinforce their confidence in the choice
waysIn.description: Bold decisions can come with quiet second-guessing, make sure they know you're fully behind the choice they made.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what makes you confident it was the right call.

templates.title: plot twist, uninvited
templates.description: A significant life change is happening that wasn't their choice, and the lack of control over it is weighing on them more than the change itself.

waysIn.tag: Sit With The Lack Of Control
waysIn.title: Don't rush toward silver linings
waysIn.description: This isn't the moment for "everything happens for a reason," let them feel the lack of control before looking for the upside.
waysIn.action: Ask what feels hardest about not having chosen this, and just listen.

templates.title: so much to figure out
templates.description: The practical side of a big life change has piled up on them, and the sheer number of moving pieces is more draining than the change itself.

waysIn.title: Handle a piece of the logistics
waysIn.description: They don't need a pep talk about change, they need one less thing on the list, offer to take on something concrete.
waysIn.action: Ask what one task you could take off their plate for this transition.

templates.title: closing a chapter, still hurts
templates.description: Even a change they mostly want comes with something being left behind, and they're quietly grieving that part more than they're showing.

waysIn.title: Let excitement and sadness coexist
waysIn.description: They're allowed to feel both hopeful and sad about the same change, don't push them to pick one over the other.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of the old chapter they'll miss the most.

templates.title: home glow-up complete
templates.description: They finished a home improvement or decorating project, and seeing their space actually reflect how they want to live is giving them real satisfaction.

waysIn.title: Give the finished space real attention
waysIn.description: A home project deserves an actual look and reaction, not a passing glance, engage with the result the way they hoped someone would.
waysIn.action: Ask them to show off the space and point out their favorite part.

templates.subScenario: Created a Space That Feels Like Home
templates.title: it finally feels like home
templates.description: Their living space has finally started to feel settled and truly theirs, and that sense of home is clearly affecting their overall mood for the better.

waysIn.title: Reflect the calm back to them
waysIn.description: Feeling settled somewhere changes a lot about daily life, name that shift specifically instead of letting it pass unspoken.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed how much more at ease they seem at home lately.

templates.title: house said "fix me"
templates.description: Something in their living space broke or needs fixing, and the hassle of dealing with it is adding stress to their day-to-day.

waysIn.title: Handle one piece of it
waysIn.description: Home repair stress is mostly logistical, offering to take on one concrete part of it helps more than sympathy alone.
waysIn.action: Offer to handle one specific task related to the repair.

templates.title: living space, spiraling
templates.description: Their living space has started to feel cluttered or chaotic, and the disorder is quietly adding to their overall stress level.

waysIn.title: Offer to tackle it as a team
waysIn.description: A messy space can feel too big to face alone, offer to work through even a small part of it together rather than suggesting they handle it.
waysIn.action: Suggest tackling one small area of the space together.

templates.title: where am I even living arc
templates.description: Something about their living situation feels uncertain, and the lack of stability is affecting how settled they feel overall.

waysIn.title: Be the constant while the space isn't
waysIn.description: When their physical space feels uncertain, being an emotionally steady presence matters even more than usual.
waysIn.action: Check in on how they're feeling about the uncertainty, not just the logistics of it.

templates.title: finally checked off
templates.description: They finally resolved something bureaucratic or administrative that had been hanging over them, and the relief of it being done is bigger than the task itself.

waysIn.title: Treat the small win as a real one
waysIn.description: Admin tasks rarely feel exciting, but finishing one that's been looming deserves genuine acknowledgment, not a shrug.
waysIn.action: Ask how it feels to finally have that off their list.

templates.title: adulting: temporarily mastered
templates.description: They set up a system or process that's made handling life admin noticeably easier, and there's real satisfaction in feeling more on top of things.

waysIn.title: Notice the order they've created
waysIn.description: Building a system that actually works takes real effort most people don't notice, point out specifically what's improved because of it.
waysIn.action: Ask what made them finally set the system up now.

templates.title: stuck in the red tape
templates.description: They're stuck dealing with a frustrating administrative or bureaucratic process, and the lack of progress is wearing on their patience.

waysIn.title: Let the annoyance be fully justified
waysIn.description: Bureaucratic frustration is uniquely draining because it's often outside their control, validate that instead of suggesting they just be patient.
waysIn.action: Let them vent about the process without offering to "just call and ask."

templates.subScenario: Overwhelmed By a Backlog of Tasks
templates.title: to-do list, out of control
templates.description: A pile of small administrative tasks has built up, and the sheer number of them is more draining than any single one on its own.

waysIn.title: Take on just one item
waysIn.description: A backlog feels less overwhelming when it's not all on them, offer to knock out one specific item rather than the whole list.
waysIn.action: Pick one task from the pile and offer to handle it or do it with them.

templates.subScenario: Missed a Deadline / Made an Admin Mistake
templates.title: deadline: missed
templates.description: They missed a deadline or made a mistake on something administrative, and they're being harder on themselves about it than the situation probably calls for.

waysIn.title: Take the harshness out of the mistake
waysIn.description: They're likely already replaying the mistake, don't add to it, remind them it's fixable and not a reflection of how capable they are.
waysIn.action: Remind them everyone misses something eventually, and help figure out the fix.

templates.title: new pet, immediate obsession
templates.description: They welcomed a new pet into their life, and the joy of it is showing up in basically every conversation they're having.

waysIn.title: Match the pet excitement fully
waysIn.description: New-pet energy is contagious for a reason, lean all the way into it instead of treating it as a minor update.
waysIn.action: Ask for a full update on the new pet, no detail too small.

templates.title: their pet did a thing
templates.description: Their pet hit a milestone or did something that made them unreasonably proud, and that specific kind of pet-parent joy is very real.

waysIn.title: Don't downplay the pet win
waysIn.description: Pet pride deserves to be taken as seriously as they're feeling it, engage with genuine enthusiasm instead of a polite "aw."
waysIn.action: Ask them to tell the full story of what happened.

templates.title: pet came through emotionally
templates.description: Their pet showed up for them emotionally in a way that made a hard moment easier, and that bond is clearly something they lean on.

waysIn.title: Respect what the pet gives them
waysIn.description: The comfort a pet provides is real and valid, acknowledge that bond instead of treating it as secondary to human support.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's clear how much their pet means to them.

templates.title: worried about their pet
templates.description: Something health-related came up with their pet, and the worry over it is sitting heavier on them than they might be showing.

waysIn.tag: Take It As Seriously As They Do
waysIn.title: Don't minimize the worry
waysIn.description: Worry over a pet's health is real worry, not an overreaction, meet it with the same seriousness you would for any loved one.
waysIn.action: Check in specifically about how the pet is doing, not just how they're holding up.

templates.title: pet parenting: hard mode
templates.description: Their pet has been going through a difficult behavioral stretch, and the frustration of not being able to fix it is wearing on them.

waysIn.title: Offer to help with the pet directly
waysIn.description: Pet-related stress often needs practical support, not just sympathy, offer to actually help with the pet itself.
