waysIn.action: Offer to take something pet-related off their hands for the day.

templates.title: missing a piece of the family
templates.description: They lost a pet, and the grief of it is real and significant, even if it's not always treated that way by everyone around them.

waysIn.title: Treat the grief with full weight
waysIn.description: This kind of loss deserves the same care as any other grief, don't minimize it or rush them toward feeling better.
waysIn.action: Simply be present with them, without trying to fix the sadness or offer a replacement.

templates.title: did good, felt good
templates.description: They spent time volunteering or helping out in their community, and it clearly left them with a genuine sense of purpose and fulfillment.

waysIn.title: Name what it says about them
waysIn.description: Giving back says something real about who they are, point that out directly instead of treating it as just a nice thing they did.
waysIn.action: Ask what part of the experience felt the most meaningful.

templates.subScenario: Made a Real Difference for Someone
templates.title: main character, side quest: helped someone
templates.description: They did something specific that made a real difference for someone else, and knowing it actually mattered is clearly sitting well with them.

waysIn.title: Point out the real impact
waysIn.description: The impact of helping someone else is easy to downplay after the fact, name specifically what it meant instead of letting it go unremarked.
waysIn.action: Tell them exactly why what they did mattered.

templates.subScenario: Disappointed By a Cause or Community
templates.title: the cause let them down
templates.description: Something about a community or cause they care about didn't live up to what they expected, and the disillusionment is bigger than they're letting on.

waysIn.title: Let the letdown be real
waysIn.description: Caring about something and being let down by it is genuinely disappointing, don't rush to defend the cause or minimize how they feel.
waysIn.action: Ask what specifically felt off, and just listen without offering a fix.

templates.subScenario: Burned Out From Overcommitting to Others
templates.title: poured out, nothing left
templates.description: They've been giving a lot of time and energy to helping others, and it's started to come at the cost of their own energy and bandwidth.

waysIn.title: Let them be taken care of for once
waysIn.description: They're used to being the one who shows up for everyone else, make this a moment where they get to be on the receiving end instead.
waysIn.action: Do something for them without them having to ask or plan it.

templates.title: neighborhood, actually pleasant
templates.description: They had a genuinely nice interaction with a neighbor, and it left them with a small but real sense of goodwill about where they live.

waysIn.title: Let the small moment matter
waysIn.description: Small good moments in daily life count too, treat it as a genuine positive instead of something too minor to mention.
waysIn.action: Ask what happened, small local stories are still good stories.

templates.title: neighborhood era: unlocked
templates.description: They're starting to feel a real sense of belonging in their local area, familiar faces, a favorite spot, that comfortable feeling of it becoming home.

waysIn.title: Notice the sense of belonging
waysIn.description: Feeling at home in a place takes time to build, acknowledge that shift instead of treating it as just geography.
waysIn.action: Ask what's made the neighborhood start to feel more like home.

templates.title: neighborhood beef, unofficial
templates.description: Some tension with a neighbor has been bothering them, and the awkwardness of an ongoing, unresolved friction so close to home is wearing on them.

waysIn.title: Be the calm inside the friction
waysIn.description: Conflict close to home is hard to fully escape, make sure being with you feels like a break from it, not another thing to manage.
waysIn.action: Ask if they want to vent about it or just want a distraction from it.

templates.title: lives here, doesn't feel like it
templates.description: They've noticed they don't feel very connected to the area they live in, more like they're just passing through than actually rooted there.

waysIn.title: Create a reason to feel rooted
waysIn.description: A sense of belonging often starts small, help create one local ritual or habit together rather than treating it as a bigger problem to solve.
waysIn.action: Suggest trying a new local spot together to start building that sense of place.

templates.title: technology said "you're welcome"
templates.description: A piece of technology they got is actually making their daily life noticeably easier, and the novelty of that convenience still has them a little delighted.

waysIn.title: Notice the small daily improvements
waysIn.description: New tech excitement fades fast once it becomes routine, point out the improvement now while they're still appreciating it.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been the best part of using it so far.

templates.title: outsmarted the technology
templates.description: They finally solved a tech issue that had been annoying them for a while, and there's real satisfaction in having figured it out themselves.

waysIn.title: Treat it like the win it is
waysIn.description: Solving an annoying tech problem takes real patience, acknowledge the effort instead of treating it as no big deal now that it's fixed.
waysIn.action: Ask how they finally figured out the fix.

templates.title: technology said no
templates.description: A piece of technology they rely on failed on them, and beyond the inconvenience, the disruption to their routine is adding real stress.

waysIn.title: Take on a piece of the fix
waysIn.description: Tech failures are mostly a logistics problem, offering to help troubleshoot or handle a piece of it matters more than sympathy alone.
waysIn.action: Offer to help troubleshoot or research a fix together.

templates.title: technology: undefeated
templates.description: They've been struggling to keep up with a piece of technology, and the frustration of feeling behind is bigger than the tech issue itself.

waysIn.title: Make struggling with tech feel normal
waysIn.description: Feeling behind on tech can feel embarrassing in a way that's disproportionate to the actual issue, normalize it instead of making it feel like a bigger deal.
waysIn.action: Offer to sit with them and figure it out together, no judgment.

templates.title: too many pings, not enough peace
templates.description: The constant pull of notifications and digital noise has been wearing on them, and they're clearly craving a quieter, less plugged-in stretch of time.

waysIn.title: Offer a low-notification window
waysIn.description: They probably won't unplug on their own, make it easy by creating a specific stretch of low-notification time together.
waysIn.action: Suggest putting phones away together for a set stretch of time.

templates.title: date night, certified
templates.description: You two had one of those date nights that reminds you why you like doing life together, easy, fun, no effort required to enjoy each other.

waysIn.title: Plan the next one before the glow fades
waysIn.description: Good date nights build momentum, use this while it's fresh instead of waiting for another one to organically happen.
waysIn.action: Ask what made that time feel so easy, then do more of exactly that.

templates.title: said the real thing
templates.description: You two had a conversation that went deeper than the usual surface-level check-ins, and it left you both feeling more known by each other.

waysIn.title: Keep that door open
waysIn.description: Vulnerability like that took some courage from both of you, make sure the response to it is more openness, not a return to autopilot.
waysIn.action: Bring up something from that conversation again, to show it actually landed.

templates.title: argument, resolved together
templates.description: You two worked through a disagreement and came out the other side actually closer, not just avoiding the topic until it faded.

waysIn.title: Notice what worked
waysIn.description: However you two got through it, name what worked so you both remember it for next time, instead of letting the resolution go unspoken.
waysIn.action: Tell your partner one thing they did during the resolution that you appreciated.

templates.subScenario: Supported Each Other Through Something Hard
templates.title: showed up for each other
templates.description: You two leaned on each other through something difficult, and the sense of being a real team came through clearly in how you handled it.

waysIn.title: Call out what worked
waysIn.description: Being a good team under pressure is worth naming out loud, not just moving on once the hard part is over.
waysIn.action: Tell your partner specifically what it meant to have them show up like that.

templates.title: we're just built different, together
templates.description: You two had one of those genuinely fun, silly moments that reminded you both how easy it is to enjoy each other's company.

waysIn.title: Bring that energy back on purpose
waysIn.description: Playful moments like that don't have to be accidental, look for a reason to recreate that same lighthearted energy.
waysIn.action: Bring up the joke or moment again just to make each other laugh about it.

templates.title: you two, on opposite sides
templates.description: You two got into it with each other, and whatever's underneath the disagreement is clearly still unresolved between you.

waysIn.title: Revisit it once things cool down
waysIn.description: This isn't about winning the argument, it's about actually resolving what caused it, come back to it once emotions aren't running the conversation.
waysIn.action: Ask your partner what they need in order to feel like this is actually resolved.

templates.title: said one thing, heard another
templates.description: Something got lost in translation between you two, and the misunderstanding is creating more distance than the actual issue probably deserves.

waysIn.title: Ask instead of assuming
waysIn.description: The gap here is probably smaller than it feels, closing it starts with asking what your partner actually meant, not assuming the worst version.
waysIn.action: Ask your partner to explain what they meant, without getting defensive first.

templates.title: you two, different frequencies
templates.description: You two have been feeling a little out of step with each other, less like a natural rhythm and more like you're both just going through the motions.

waysIn.title: Make deliberate time to sync back up
waysIn.description: Feeling out of sync usually fixes itself with intention, not time, make a deliberate effort to reconnect instead of waiting for it to pass.
waysIn.action: Plan real, undistracted time together with no other agenda.

templates.title: didn't show up the way they needed
templates.description: One of you let the other down in a way that's still sitting between you, and the disappointment hasn't fully been addressed yet.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge it plainly
waysIn.description: This needs a direct acknowledgment more than an explanation, own the specific way you fell short before moving toward fixing it.
waysIn.action: Apologize specifically for what happened, without adding a "but."

templates.title: not the plan either of you had in mind
templates.description: Something you two had planned together didn't go how either of you expected, and the disappointment is sitting a little heavier than the plan itself would suggest.

waysIn.title: Give the plan another shot
waysIn.description: The disappointment is really about the missed expectation, not the logistics, address that directly and offer to try again properly.
waysIn.action: Suggest a redo of the plan, addressing what went wrong.

templates.title: main character confidence, unlocked
templates.description: They've been trusting their own judgment more, less second-guessing, more just deciding and moving forward without needing outside validation first.

waysIn.title: Reflect their growth back to them
waysIn.description: This shift is worth naming, they might not fully see it themselves yet, point out specifically what's different in how they're carrying themselves.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed they seem more sure of themselves.

templates.title: told themselves they could, then did
templates.description: They did something they weren't sure they were capable of, and proving it to themselves has quietly shifted how they see their own abilities.

waysIn.title: Point out what this proves about them
waysIn.description: This kind of internal proof is powerful but easy to downplay, reflect back exactly what this says about their capability.
waysIn.action: Remind them of this moment the next time they start doubting themselves about something else.

templates.title: unbothered, in the best way
templates.description: They've been feeling genuinely at ease with who they are, less performing for others, more just being themselves without apology.

waysIn.title: Let them know their real self is enough
waysIn.description: This ease is worth protecting, reinforce that you like them exactly as they're showing up.
waysIn.action: Tell them something specific you appreciate about how authentically they've been showing up.

templates.title: confidence: buffering
templates.description: They've been second-guessing themselves more than usual, questioning decisions and abilities that they normally wouldn't think twice about.

waysIn.title: Remind them what's actually true
waysIn.description: Self-doubt distorts how someone sees their own ability, counter it with something specific and true, not generic reassurance.
waysIn.action: Tell them a specific thing you know they're good at, and why.

templates.title: waiting to be found out
templates.description: Despite doing well by any outside measure, they've been feeling like they don't actually deserve it, like it's only a matter of time before someone notices.

waysIn.title: Point out the gap between feeling and fact
waysIn.description: Imposter syndrome thrives on staying unspoken, gently name the gap between how they feel and what's actually true.
waysIn.action: Remind them of specific evidence that contradicts the feeling.

templates.title: one mistake, spiraling confidence
templates.description: A mistake they made has shaken their confidence more broadly, turning one moment into a bigger story about their overall competence.

waysIn.title: Keep the mistake in its lane
waysIn.description: One mistake doesn't define overall ability, help them keep the mistake sized correctly instead of letting it spread into a bigger narrative.
waysIn.action: Remind them of a time they made a mistake and it didn't actually change anything between you.

templates.title: main character, on a mission
templates.description: They've been in one of those stretches where everything just feels doable, driven and focused in a way that's clearly energizing them.

waysIn.title: Feed the drive without adding pressure
waysIn.description: This energy is good to be around, support it by staying out of the way rather than adding your own goals or expectations onto it.
waysIn.action: Ask what's got them feeling so driven.

templates.title: remembered why they started
templates.description: After feeling a little aimless, they've reconnected with the actual reason behind what they're working toward, and it's clearly reignited something in them.

waysIn.title: Let them talk through what clicked
waysIn.description: This kind of internal shift is worth hearing about in their own words, ask genuinely rather than assuming you already know what changed.
waysIn.action: Ask what helped them reconnect with their motivation.

templates.title: motivated by themselves, for themselves
templates.description: They've shifted toward doing things because they actually want to, not because of outside pressure or expectation, and it's changing how sustainable their effort feels.

waysIn.title: Praise the motive, not just the output
waysIn.description: This shift toward internal motivation is worth protecting, praise the reason behind what they're doing, not just what they're producing.
waysIn.action: Tell them you can tell this one actually matters to them personally.

templates.title: motivation left the chat
templates.description: Their usual drive has quietly disappeared, and even things they normally care about are starting to feel like a struggle to want to do.

waysIn.title: Let low motivation be okay for now
waysIn.description: Trying to motivate someone out of a slump often backfires, take the pressure off instead of pushing them toward productivity.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing something low-stakes and enjoyable with zero productivity attached.

templates.title: motivation existential crisis
templates.description: They've been questioning why they should even bother with things they used to care about, more numbness than clear sadness behind it.

waysIn.title: Sit with the questioning instead of solving it
waysIn.description: This isn't something to talk them out of quickly, sit with the questioning alongside them instead of jumping straight to reasons things matter.
waysIn.action: Ask what's underneath the feeling, without trying to immediately counter it.

templates.title: effort tank: empty
templates.description: They've been putting in effort for a while without much payoff, and the exhaustion of continuing to try is starting to outweigh the drive itself.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge how long they've been pushing
waysIn.description: They probably need the effort itself acknowledged, not a reminder to keep going, name how long they've been carrying this.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's okay to ease off for a bit, without any conditions attached.

templates.title: direction: locked in
templates.description: They've been feeling unusually clear about where they're headed in life, less drifting, more a real sense of what they're building toward.

waysIn.title: Show interest in where they're headed
waysIn.description: Clarity like this deserves genuine curiosity, ask about the direction itself rather than only the practical next steps.
waysIn.action: Ask them to describe what they're working toward, in their own words.

templates.title: life finally making sense
templates.description: Different parts of their life are feeling like they're pointing in the same direction, and that sense of alignment is giving them real peace.

waysIn.title: Reflect the coherence back to them
waysIn.description: This feeling of things fitting together is worth naming, point out what you've noticed lining up for them.
waysIn.action: Tell them what you've noticed feels more settled about them lately.

templates.title: found purpose in the plot twist
templates.description: They found a sense of meaning in something they didn't expect to, and it's shifted how they think about what matters to them.

waysIn.title: Ask what changed their perspective
waysIn.description: This kind of discovery deserves real curiosity, ask genuinely what led them there instead of assuming it's obvious.
waysIn.action: Ask what about it feels meaningful to them now.

templates.title: wandering, no map
templates.description: They've been feeling like they're just going through the motions without a clear sense of where any of it is leading.

waysIn.title: Let the uncertainty exist without fixing it
waysIn.description: Feeling aimless doesn't need to be solved immediately, resist the urge to suggest a plan and just let them sit with the uncertainty.
waysIn.action: Ask what feels most unclear, and just listen without offering direction.

templates.title: wondering if this is even the right road
templates.description: They've been quietly questioning whether the path they're on is actually the one they want, more uncertainty than crisis, but it's sitting with them.

waysIn.title: Don't rush toward an answer
waysIn.description: This isn't a question that needs solving, be a sounding board without pushing them toward a decision before they're ready.
waysIn.action: Ask what's prompting the doubt, and let them think out loud.

templates.title: now what
templates.description: After reaching something they'd been working toward for a long time, they've been left with an unexpected emptiness instead of the satisfaction they expected.

waysIn.title: Name the anticlimax without minimizing it
waysIn.description: This "now what" feeling after a big accomplishment is more common than people admit, validate it instead of questioning why they aren't happier.
waysIn.action: Ask what they're curious about exploring next, with no pressure to have an answer.

templates.title: grateful, no notes
templates.description: They've been feeling a real, settled appreciation for their life as it is, less chasing the next thing, more just soaking in what's already good.

waysIn.title: Match the contentment, don't disrupt it
waysIn.description: This kind of quiet gratitude doesn't need fixing or amplifying, just be present with them in it instead of introducing something new to chase.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been standing out to them as something they're grateful for.

templates.title: finding joy in the little stuff
templates.description: Ordinary, small moments have been landing more meaningfully for them lately, and there's a lightness in how present they seem to be with the everyday.

waysIn.tag: Point Out A Small Thing Too
waysIn.title: Add to the noticing
waysIn.description: This mindset feeds on itself, point out a small good thing yourself to reinforce the pattern rather than only observing it.
waysIn.action: Mention one small thing you've appreciated recently, to keep the energy going.

templates.title: not chasing anything
templates.description: They've reached a place of feeling like what they have is genuinely enough, without the usual pull toward the next goal or upgrade.

waysIn.title: Don't introduce a new goal
waysIn.description: This contentment is rare and worth protecting, resist the instinct to suggest what's next and just let this feeling be complete on its own.
waysIn.action: Tell them you love seeing them this settled, full stop, no follow-up question about what's next.

templates.title: hedonic treadmill, fully engaged
templates.description: No matter what they achieve or get, satisfaction never seems to stick, and the constant chase for the next thing is starting to feel exhausting even to them.

waysIn.title: Point out the cycle without judgment
waysIn.description: This pattern is easier to see from the outside, name it gently as an observation rather than a criticism of how they're living.
waysIn.action: Ask them to name one thing that already feels like enough.

templates.title: always somewhere else mentally
templates.description: They've been so focused on what's ahead that the present moment keeps slipping by mostly unnoticed and unappreciated.

waysIn.title: Pull their focus to right here
waysIn.description: They probably won't slow down on their own, create a moment that gently pulls their attention into the present instead of the future.
waysIn.action: Plan something simple that has no purpose beyond just being enjoyable.

templates.title: future's looking bright, actually
templates.description: They've been feeling genuinely optimistic about what's ahead, less bracing for things to go wrong, more real excitement about what's coming.

waysIn.title: Get specific about the future with them
waysIn.description: Hope feels more real when it's specific, ask about the details of what they're looking forward to instead of a general "that's great."
waysIn.action: Ask what part of the future they're most excited about.

templates.title: dreaming a little bigger lately
templates.description: They've been letting themselves imagine bigger possibilities for their life, and there's an openness to what could happen that wasn't there before.

waysIn.title: Treat the possibility as real
waysIn.description: Big dreams are fragile when they're new, take what they're imagining seriously instead of gently grounding it in practicality too soon.
waysIn.action: Ask them to describe the possibility in more detail, without steering it toward logistics.

templates.title: future anxiety, fully loaded
templates.description: They've been feeling uneasy about what's coming, more focused on what could go wrong than on any of the possible good outcomes.

waysIn.title: Shrink the future back down to now
waysIn.description: Worry about the future often grows bigger than what's actually in front of them, help bring their focus back to something manageable and immediate.
waysIn.action: Ask what's the one thing about the future that's weighing on them most.

templates.subScenario: Feeling Stuck With No Way Forward
templates.title: future feels like a dead end
templates.description: They've been feeling like there's no clear way forward from where they are, and that sense of being stuck is heavier than a normal rough patch.

waysIn.title: Be present in the stuck feeling
waysIn.description: This isn't a moment for a five-step plan, be present with how stuck it feels before jumping to ways out.
waysIn.action: Ask them to describe what stuck feels like, without offering solutions yet.

templates.title: scared of the same thing happening again
templates.description: They've been carrying a quiet fear that something difficult from before is going to happen again, and it's coloring how they think about what's ahead.

waysIn.title: Name it instead of reassuring past it
waysIn.description: Vague reassurance rarely lands here, naming the specific fear plainly does more than telling them not to worry.
waysIn.action: Ask them directly what they're afraid might repeat, and just listen.

templates.title: emotionally unbothered, in a good way
templates.description: They've been navigating their emotions with more ease lately, feeling things fully without getting swept away by them the way they sometimes do.

waysIn.title: Reflect their composure back to them
waysIn.description: This kind of emotional steadiness is easy to take for granted, name it specifically so they know it's actually showing.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed how level they've been handling things lately.

templates.title: felt it, then moved through it
templates.description: They moved through a genuinely hard emotion in a healthy way, giving it space instead of pushing it down or getting stuck in it.

waysIn.title: Name the growth in how they handled it
waysIn.description: How they handled this says something real about their emotional growth, point that out instead of only focusing on the situation itself.
waysIn.action: Tell them you noticed how well they moved through that.

templates.title: emotions: at capacity
templates.description: They've been feeling emotionally overwhelmed, like everything is hitting at once and there's no space to process any of it properly.

waysIn.title: Simplify what's around them
waysIn.description: They don't need more to process, reduce demands on them where you can instead of adding anything new to the pile.
waysIn.action: Take something off their plate, anything that reduces the load.

templates.title: holding it together, barely
templates.description: They've been pushing their feelings down instead of dealing with them, and the effort of holding it together is starting to show through the cracks.

waysIn.title: Open a door without forcing it
waysIn.description: They probably won't open up if pushed, create a low-pressure opening and let them decide whether to walk through it.
waysIn.action: Let them know you're around if they want to talk, then genuinely let it be their choice.

templates.title: patience running thin
templates.description: Their emotional reactions have been bigger and quicker than usual, more snapping than their normal, more even-keeled self.

waysIn.title: Recognize it's not really about you
waysIn.description: A short fuse usually means something else is going on underneath, respond to the underlying stress rather than reacting to the snap itself.
waysIn.action: Give them some space first, then check in gently once things have settled.

templates.title: stopped fighting themselves
templates.description: They've made real peace with something about themselves they used to be hard on, and there's a noticeable lightness in no longer fighting that part of who they are.

waysIn.title: Echo their own acceptance back
waysIn.description: This kind of self-acceptance deserves reinforcement, agree with their own kinder view of themselves instead of staying neutral.
waysIn.action: Tell them you love that particular thing about them, the one they used to be hard on themselves about.

templates.title: flawed and thriving
templates.description: They've been letting go of the need to have everything figured out or perfect, and there's real relief in allowing themselves to just be a work in progress.

waysIn.title: Make imperfection feel welcome
waysIn.description: This shift needs reinforcement, not correction, let them know being a work in progress around you is completely fine.
waysIn.action: Share something imperfect about yourself too, to make the acceptance feel mutual.

templates.title: their own worst critic, again
templates.description: Their self-talk has been unusually harsh lately, holding themselves to a standard they'd never expect from anyone else.

waysIn.title: Offer a kinder narrator
waysIn.description: They're stuck hearing only the harsh voice, offer the kinder perspective they're not giving themselves.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what you'd say to a friend in their position, then say it to them.

templates.title: enoughness: questioning it
templates.description: They've been carrying a nagging feeling that they're falling short somehow, even without a specific event pointing to why.

waysIn.title: State it plainly, without qualifiers
waysIn.description: Vague feelings of not being enough need a direct, specific counter, not general reassurance, tell them plainly why they're enough as they are.
waysIn.action: Tell them one specific way they matter to you, no qualifiers attached.

templates.subScenario: Struggling to Accept Change in Themselves
templates.title: not recognizing themselves lately
templates.description: They've noticed themselves changing in some way and are struggling to accept it, holding onto an older version of who they used to be.

waysIn.title: Show them the new version is still loved
waysIn.description: Change can feel like a loss of identity, reassure them that who they're becoming is just as welcome as who they were.
waysIn.action: Tell them something you appreciate about how they've changed.

templates.title: brain fog: cleared
templates.description: Their thinking has felt unusually clear lately, decisions coming easier, thoughts more organized than the usual mental clutter.

waysIn.title: Take advantage of the clear-headedness
waysIn.description: Clear thinking is a good window for real conversations, take advantage of it rather than saving important talks for a foggier day.
waysIn.action: Ask if there's something on their mind they'd want to talk through while things feel clear.

templates.title: lightbulb moment, fully lit
templates.description: Something clicked for them mentally, a realization that suddenly made sense of something they'd been turning over for a while.

waysIn.title: Ask them to walk you through it
waysIn.description: New realizations solidify when explained out loud, ask them to walk you through the thinking rather than just hearing the conclusion.
waysIn.action: Ask what led them to that realization.

templates.title: brain fog, thick
templates.description: Their thinking has felt cloudy and slow lately, small decisions taking more effort than they should and focus slipping more than usual.

waysIn.title: Reduce the decisions they have to make
waysIn.description: Mental fog gets worse when there's more to think about, take small decisions off their hands rather than asking them to figure things out.
waysIn.action: Decide something small for them, so it's one less thing they have to think through.

templates.title: attention, everywhere at once
templates.description: Their focus has been scattered across too many things, and the inability to settle on one thing is leaving them mentally exhausted.

waysIn.title: Give them one thing to land on
waysIn.description: A scattered mind needs a single point to settle on, not more options, offer one simple, grounding activity rather than a list of choices.
waysIn.action: Suggest one specific, simple thing to focus on together, nothing that requires more decisions.

templates.title: nervous system: chill
templates.description: They've been feeling a real sense of calm lately, less internal noise, more just being okay with wherever things currently stand.

waysIn.title: Don't introduce unnecessary stress
waysIn.description: This calm is worth safeguarding, avoid stirring up anything unnecessary and let them enjoy the quiet while it's here.
waysIn.action: Suggest something low-key that keeps the peaceful mood going.

templates.subScenario: Found Stillness After a Busy Stretch
templates.title: nervous system, off high alert
templates.description: After a stretch of being wound up, they've finally found some real stillness, and the difference in how they're holding themselves is noticeable.

waysIn.title: Don't rush them back into motion
waysIn.description: This stillness is fragile after a busy period, resist filling their time back up too quickly and let them enjoy the slower pace.
waysIn.action: Suggest doing absolutely nothing together for a while, no agenda.

templates.title: restlessness, no clear cause
templates.description: They've been feeling internally restless, a low hum of unease that doesn't seem tied to any one specific thing.

waysIn.title: Give their restlessness somewhere to land
waysIn.description: Vague restlessness responds better to grounding than distraction, offer something calm and physical rather than more stimulation.
waysIn.action: Suggest a simple, physical activity that gives their restless energy somewhere to go.

templates.title: inner conflict, no ceasefire yet
templates.description: They've been caught in some kind of internal back-and-forth, torn between two feelings or decisions without clear resolution.

waysIn.title: Don't push them toward one side
waysIn.description: They don't need you picking a side of their internal conflict, just make space for them to sit with the tension until it resolves on its own.
waysIn.action: Ask them to talk through both sides of what they're feeling, without steering toward either one.

templates.title: someone finally gets it
templates.description: They've had the experience of feeling genuinely understood recently, like someone actually got what they meant without needing it over-explained.

waysIn.title: Reinforce that you get it too
waysIn.description: Feeling understood is rare enough to actively nurture, show them you're tracking with them too, not just that you heard the words.
waysIn.action: Reflect back something they've said recently in your own words, to show it landed.

templates.title: said it exactly as it is
templates.description: They've felt comfortable being completely honest about something without softening or editing it, and that freedom is clearly a relief.

waysIn.title: Respond in a way that welcomes more
waysIn.description: How you respond to this honesty determines whether they keep offering it, meet it with openness rather than any hint of judgment.
waysIn.action: Thank them specifically for being that honest with you.

templates.title: said it, still not landing
templates.description: They've felt like what they're actually trying to say isn't coming across, and the gap between their intent and how it's being received is frustrating them.

waysIn.title: Check your own understanding first
waysIn.description: The instinct to explain your side can make this worse, ask what they actually mean before responding to what you think they mean.
waysIn.action: Ask them to explain it again, in a different way, and really listen closely.

templates.title: feels like a solo experience
templates.description: They've been feeling like no one around them really understands what they're going through, even if people are technically present and supportive.

waysIn.tag: Sit In It, Don't Explain It Away
waysIn.title: Don't rush to relate
waysIn.description: This isn't the moment to compare it to your own experience, just witness what they're going through without trying to make it feel less isolating through comparison.
waysIn.action: Tell them you don't need to fully understand it to be there for them.

templates.title: glow-up, self-aware edition
templates.description: They've been noticing real growth in themselves compared to who they used to be, and there's quiet pride in recognizing how far they've come.

waysIn.title: Validate the growth they're noticing
waysIn.description: Self-recognized growth means more when someone else confirms it, agree with specifics rather than a generic "you've grown so much."
waysIn.action: Tell them a specific way you've noticed them grow.

templates.title: unlocked a new level of self-knowledge
templates.description: They've had a genuine insight into how they work, a pattern or truth about themselves that they hadn't clearly seen before.

waysIn.title: Engage with what they learned
waysIn.description: This kind of self-discovery deserves real engagement, ask follow-up questions instead of a quick acknowledgment and moving on.
waysIn.action: Ask how this new understanding might change how they approach things going forward.

templates.title: déjà vu, but make it a bad habit
templates.description: They've noticed themselves repeating a pattern they thought they'd moved past, and the frustration of feeling stuck in old behavior is wearing on them.

waysIn.title: Separate awareness from failure
waysIn.description: Noticing a pattern is actually progress, even if it doesn't feel like it, reframe the awareness itself as a step forward, not a setback.
waysIn.action: Point out that noticing the pattern at all is different from where they used to be.

templates.title: growth arc, buffering
templates.description: They've been feeling impatient with how slowly they seem to be changing or improving, expecting more progress than what feels visible.

waysIn.title: Reflect the longer timeline
waysIn.description: Growth is hard to see up close, help them zoom out to a longer timeline where the change actually becomes visible.
waysIn.action: Remind them of something specific about themselves that's genuinely different from a while back.

templates.title: zoomed out, feeling good about it
templates.description: They've been feeling a genuine sense of connection to something larger than their day-to-day, and it's giving them a calm, grounded perspective.

waysIn.title: Engage with the bigger-picture thinking
waysIn.description: This kind of reflection deserves real engagement, ask about it with genuine curiosity instead of steering the conversation back to practical matters.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been giving them that bigger-picture sense of peace.

templates.subScenario: Found Clarity On What Truly Matters
templates.title: figured out the actual priorities
templates.description: They've reached a clearer sense of what genuinely matters to them, cutting through a lot of noise that used to feel important but isn't anymore.

waysIn.title: Show you're paying attention to their priorities
waysIn.description: This clarity is worth reflecting in how you show up for them, not just acknowledging it in conversation.
waysIn.action: Ask them to share what's risen to the top of their priorities lately.

templates.title: thinking about the bigger stuff again
templates.description: They've been sitting with some bigger, harder-to-answer questions about life and meaning, more contemplative than distressed, but it's taking up real mental space.

waysIn.title: Don't rush to resolve the question
waysIn.description: Big questions like this don't need quick answers, be a thinking partner rather than trying to wrap it up with a tidy conclusion.
waysIn.action: Ask what's been prompting the bigger questions, and just explore it together.

templates.title: searching for the point of it all
templates.description: Things that used to feel meaningful haven't been landing the same way, and they're quietly searching for something to reconnect them to a sense of significance.

waysIn.title: Point back to something that used to matter
waysIn.description: Bring up something specific that used to feel meaningful to them, as a gentle reminder rather than a solution.
waysIn.action: Ask what used to feel meaningful, and whether any of it still resonates.

templates.subScenario: Discovering A New Side of Themselves
templates.title: plot twist: new side of themselves
templates.description: They've discovered a side of themselves they didn't fully know was there, and there's genuine excitement in expanding how they see themselves.

waysIn.title: Make room for the discovery
waysIn.description: New sides of identity need room to be explored, meet this new layer with curiosity rather than comparing it to who they were before.
waysIn.action: Ask them more about this new side they're discovering.

templates.subScenario: Feeling Solid In Who They Are
templates.title: identity: fully loaded and confirmed
templates.description: They've reached a stretch of feeling really clear and solid about who they are, less shaped by outside opinions, more just being themselves confidently.

waysIn.title: Affirm the clarity you see
waysIn.description: This groundedness is worth naming, tell them specifically what feels different about how solid they seem.
waysIn.action: Tell them you can tell they know exactly who they are lately.

templates.title: identity crisis, soft launch
templates.description: They've been feeling unclear about who they are, caught between an old version of themselves and someone they haven't fully become yet.

waysIn.title: Let the in-between be okay
waysIn.description: This kind of identity confusion doesn't resolve quickly, resist offering a label or answer and just let them sit in the in-between.
waysIn.action: Ask what parts of themselves feel true, without needing a full picture yet.

templates.title: misplaced their own personality
templates.description: They've noticed a gap between who they used to be and who they feel like now, and the disconnect from their old self is unsettling them.

waysIn.title: Reflect back the parts still there
waysIn.description: They probably feel like something's missing, point out the parts of them that are still recognizably, consistently them.
waysIn.action: Tell them something about who they are that hasn't changed, even now.

templates.title: nostalgia hitting soft and warm
templates.description: They've been thinking fondly about an earlier chapter of their life, and revisiting those memories has been giving them a genuine, warm kind of comfort.

waysIn.tag: Wander Down Memory Lane With Them
waysIn.title: Ask to hear the memory
waysIn.description: Nostalgic moments are more enjoyable when shared, ask them to tell you about it instead of letting them sit with it alone.
waysIn.action: Ask them to tell you more about the memory they've been thinking about.

templates.title: looking back, liking the glow-up
templates.description: They've been comparing where they are now to an earlier version of themselves, and feeling genuinely good about the distance they've traveled.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge the full arc, not just the destination
waysIn.description: This kind of reflection deserves acknowledgment of the whole journey, not just where they've landed, name the growth across the arc.
waysIn.action: Ask what feels most different about who they are now compared to then.

templates.title: wishing for a rewind button
templates.description: They've been wishing things could go back to how they were at an earlier point, and the longing for that time is tinged with a quiet sadness about now.

waysIn.title: Let the wish be understandable
waysIn.description: This isn't a feeling to talk them out of, acknowledge why that earlier time made sense to miss instead of redirecting to the present too quickly.
waysIn.action: Ask what specifically they miss most about that time.

templates.subScenario: Comparing Present Unfavorably to the Past
templates.title: things used to feel easier
templates.description: They've been measuring their current situation against an earlier period and feeling like things have gotten harder or less good by comparison.

waysIn.title: Add context they might be missing
waysIn.description: The past often gets remembered more simply than it actually was, gently offer a fuller picture without dismissing how hard things feel now.
waysIn.action: Ask what would need to be true for things to feel as good as they did back then.

templates.title: anxiety took the day off
templates.description: Their usual background hum of worry has quieted down lately, and the mental space that's opened up from that is clearly making things feel easier.

waysIn.title: Don't introduce new worries
waysIn.description: This calmer stretch is worth protecting, be mindful of not bringing up anything unnecessarily worry-inducing.
waysIn.action: Suggest something relaxed that keeps the easier energy going.

templates.subScenario: Managed Anxiety Well In the Moment
templates.title: anxiety showed up, they showed up harder
templates.description: They faced a moment that would normally spike their anxiety and handled it with more ease than they expected, and there's real pride in that.

waysIn.title: Name the specific moment of coping well
waysIn.description: This is a concrete win worth naming specifically, point out exactly what they did differently instead of a general "good job."
waysIn.action: Tell them you noticed how well they handled that moment.

templates.title: worry, running in the background
templates.description: They've had a constant, low-grade sense of worry running underneath everything, not tied to one clear thing but present nonetheless.

waysIn.title: Offer steadiness, not solutions
waysIn.description: Diffuse anxiety doesn't have one fix, being a calm, steady presence helps more than trying to identify and solve the exact cause.
waysIn.action: Suggest a calming activity together with no pressure to talk about what's causing it.

templates.title: pre-worrying about the worry
templates.description: They've been anxious about something upcoming well before it's actually happened, spending more energy dreading it than the event will likely require.

waysIn.title: Bring focus back to the present
waysIn.description: Anticipatory anxiety grows the longer it's left unaddressed, help bring their attention back to the present instead of the looming future moment.
waysIn.action: Distract with something engaging that takes their mind off the wait.

templates.title: nervous system: on edge
templates.description: Their anxiety has been showing up physically, tension, restlessness, that keyed-up feeling in the body, more than just mental worry.

waysIn.title: Offer something physically calming
waysIn.description: When anxiety shows up in the body, physical calm often helps more than conversation, offer something soothing and low-key rather than talking it through.
waysIn.action: Suggest a physically calming activity, like a walk or something slow-paced together.

templates.title: their own best company
templates.description: They've been genuinely enjoying their own company lately, comfortable being alone with their thoughts instead of needing constant distraction or company.

waysIn.title: Don't read alone time as distance
waysIn.description: Enjoying solitude isn't a sign of pulling away, respect this as a healthy state rather than checking in like something's wrong.
waysIn.action: Let them have that time uninterrupted, and tell them you're glad they're finding peace in it.

templates.title: solo but still surrounded, energetically
templates.description: They've noticed that even in moments of solitude, they don't feel isolated, carrying a sense of connection with them regardless of who's physically around.

waysIn.title: Affirm you're part of that felt connection
waysIn.description: This is a good moment to gently affirm your place in that sense of connection, without making it about needing constant proximity.
waysIn.action: Tell them you love that they feel that way, even when you're not physically together.

templates.title: surrounded by people, feeling alone anyway
templates.description: They've been feeling isolated even in moments with other people around, like something about real connection is missing despite the company.

waysIn.title: Offer actual connection, not just proximity
waysIn.description: Physical presence alone won't fix this, offer genuine, focused attention rather than just being in the same room.
waysIn.action: Set aside real, undistracted time together, phones away, full attention.

templates.subScenario: Feeling Unseen In Their Own Life
templates.title: feels like a background character lately
templates.description: They've been feeling like a bystander in their own life, going through the motions without feeling like anyone, including themselves, is really noticing them.

waysIn.title: Put real focus on them specifically
waysIn.description: They need to feel actively noticed, not just cared about in general, direct real, specific attention their way.
waysIn.action: Plan something that centers entirely around them and what they'd enjoy.

templates.title: surface-level, wanting deeper
templates.description: They've been craving a deeper kind of connection than what their current relationships are offering, more meaning, less small talk.

waysIn.title: Offer a more meaningful exchange
waysIn.description: This is an invitation to go beneath the surface, initiate a real conversation instead of defaulting to the usual catch-up questions.
waysIn.action: Ask them something more meaningful than the usual "how was your day."

templates.title: valuable, no achievements required
templates.description: They've been feeling genuinely good about themselves independent of what they're producing or accomplishing, and that separation feels like real relief.

waysIn.title: Praise who they are, not what they do
waysIn.description: Reinforce this shift by praising something about who they are rather than defaulting to praise about what they've accomplished.
waysIn.action: Tell them something you value about them that has nothing to do with achievement.

templates.title: secure without the spotlight
templates.description: They've felt solid in their own worth even without outside recognition backing it up, less dependent on others' approval than usual.

waysIn.tag: Confirm It Without Making It The Point
waysIn.title: Support without over-praising
waysIn.description: Offer genuine support without turning it into a big deal, since the whole point is they don't need external validation to feel secure.
waysIn.action: Just enjoy time together without commenting on any specific accomplishment.

templates.title: only feels okay when producing
templates.description: They've been feeling like their value depends on being productive or accomplishing something, and rest feels unearned instead of okay.

waysIn.title: Value them while doing nothing
waysIn.description: Show them their worth isn't tied to output by valuing them explicitly during downtime, not just when they're achieving something.
waysIn.action: Do something relaxed together and tell them you enjoy just being with them, no achievement required.

templates.title: one loss, feeling like it's everything
templates.description: A setback has made them feel like their overall worth took a hit, generalizing one disappointing outcome into a bigger statement about themselves.

waysIn.tag: Separate The Setback From Their Worth
waysIn.title: Draw a clear line
waysIn.description: Make the distinction explicit, a setback is about one moment, not their overall value, and say that plainly rather than assuming it's obvious.
waysIn.action: Remind them of their worth in a way that has nothing to do with the setback.

templates.title: bar keeps moving, apparently
templates.description: They've had a persistent sense of falling short of some standard, even when there's no clear evidence they're actually failing at anything.

waysIn.title: Question the standard itself
waysIn.description: Gently question whether the standard they're measuring against is even reasonable, rather than reassuring them they're meeting it.
waysIn.action: Ask them where that standard is even coming from, and just listen to the answer.

templates.title: brain finally let it go
templates.description: They managed to stop replaying something over and over in their head, and the mental quiet from finally letting it go feels like a real relief.

waysIn.title: Don't reopen the loop
waysIn.description: Avoid accidentally bringing the topic back up out of curiosity, protect the mental quiet they've worked to reach.
waysIn.action: Suggest something engaging enough to keep their mind pleasantly occupied.

templates.subScenario: Thought It Through, Then Moved On
templates.title: thought about it, then closed the tab
templates.description: They worked through something mentally in a healthy way and actually reached a resolution instead of getting stuck in the loop.

waysIn.title: Confirm they can put it down
waysIn.description: Let them know it's genuinely fine to be done thinking about it, rather than probing for more detail.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's great they were able to work through that and move forward.

templates.title: same thought, on repeat
templates.description: They've been replaying the same thought or scenario over and over without reaching any resolution, and the mental loop is exhausting them.

waysIn.title: Offer a genuine mental off-ramp
waysIn.description: Talking through it more can sometimes feed the loop rather than break it, offer an engaging distraction instead of another round of discussion.
waysIn.action: Suggest something that genuinely absorbs their attention elsewhere.

templates.title: turned a small thing into a whole investigation
templates.description: They've been picking apart a small interaction or moment far more than it probably warrants, searching for meaning that may not be there.

waysIn.title: Give the low-key interpretation
waysIn.description: Offer the simplest, most likely explanation without dismissing their concern outright, sometimes a small thing really is just a small thing.
waysIn.action: Share your honest, simple take on the situation, without over-explaining it.

templates.title: imagination went straight to disaster
templates.description: Their mind has been jumping to worst-case outcomes for things that haven't happened yet, and the mental energy spent bracing for bad outcomes is wearing them down.

waysIn.title: Introduce the likely outcome
waysIn.description: Gently introduce the more probable, less catastrophic version of events without dismissing the underlying worry.
waysIn.action: Ask what the most likely outcome actually is, not just the worst one.

templates.title: finally being nice to themselves
templates.description: They've been talking to and treating themselves with more kindness lately, less harsh internal dialogue, more grace for being imperfect.

waysIn.title: Reinforce the kind self-talk
waysIn.description: Reflect the same gentleness back at them, agreeing with their kinder self-view instead of staying neutral or joking about it.
waysIn.action: Tell them you've noticed they've been easier on themselves lately, and that you like it.

templates.title: forgave themselves, actually meant it
templates.description: They've genuinely forgiven themselves for something they'd been holding onto, and the release of that self-directed guilt feels real and settled.

waysIn.title: Agree the forgiveness is warranted
waysIn.description: Reinforce their self-forgiveness by agreeing it's warranted, rather than staying neutral or unintentionally reopening the old guilt.
waysIn.action: Tell them you agree, and that it really is okay now.

templates.title: giving themselves zero grace
templates.description: They've been unusually hard on themselves, holding onto a mistake or shortcoming with far less grace than they'd offer anyone else.

waysIn.title: Extend compassion on their behalf
waysIn.description: Offer the compassion they're withholding from themselves directly and specifically, rather than a general "don't be so hard on yourself."
waysIn.action: Tell them exactly what you'd say to comfort a friend in their position.

templates.title: still serving themselves the sentence
templates.description: They've been unable to move past something they feel they did wrong, holding onto self-blame long after the situation has otherwise passed.

waysIn.title: Point out the ongoing cost
waysIn.description: Gently point out how long they've been carrying this, and that continuing to punish themselves isn't changing what happened.
waysIn.action: Ask what it would take for them to feel like they've paid enough, then remind them they already have.

templates.title: emotionally turned all the way up
templates.description: They've been feeling everything more vividly lately, joy, excitement, even sadness landing with more intensity than the usual muted version of daily life.

waysIn.title: Match their emotional depth
waysIn.description: Show up with the same level of presence they're bringing, rather than responding with a flatter, more muted energy that doesn't match.
waysIn.action: Share something that made you feel deeply too, to meet their emotional openness with your own.

templates.title: dopamine from the little stuff
templates.description: Small everyday moments have been bringing them genuine joy again, a shift from feeling flat to actually feeling delighted by ordinary things.

waysIn.title: Add to the list of little delights
waysIn.description: Lean into this by intentionally creating more small, joyful moments rather than saving delight for something bigger.
waysIn.action: Do one small, simple thing together that's just for the fun of it.

templates.title: emotions on mute
templates.description: They've been feeling emotionally flat lately, going through moments that would normally bring joy or sadness without much reaction either way.

waysIn.title: Offer low-pressure emotional texture
waysIn.description: Don't force big reactions, gently offer experiences with emotional texture and let feeling come back at its own pace.
waysIn.action: Suggest something mildly stimulating and low-pressure, without expecting a big emotional response.

templates.title: present physically, checked out otherwise
templates.description: They've been moving through their days on autopilot, present in body but not really emotionally engaged with what's happening around them.

waysIn.title: Create a moment that pulls them into the present
waysIn.description: Create a low-key moment specifically designed to pull their attention and presence back into the here and now.
waysIn.action: Do something that requires their full attention, even briefly, to gently break the autopilot.

templates.title: real talk, no filter
templates.description: They've been expressing what they actually think and feel more openly lately, less editing themselves to be palatable, more just being direct.

waysIn.title: Respond well to the honesty
waysIn.description: How you respond here shapes whether this openness continues, meet directness with openness rather than defensiveness, even if it's blunt.
waysIn.action: Thank them for saying it straight, even if it wasn't what you expected to hear.

templates.subScenario: Showing Up As Their Full Self
templates.title: unfiltered and thriving
templates.description: They've been letting more of their real personality show, quirks and all, instead of the more curated version they sometimes lead with.

waysIn.title: React with genuine delight
waysIn.description: Show real enjoyment of the fuller, less edited version of them, so the instinct to hold back doesn't creep back in.
waysIn.action: Tell them specifically what you love about the unfiltered version of them.

templates.title: saying "fine" instead of the truth
templates.description: They've been holding back what they actually think or feel, defaulting to easier, safer responses instead of saying what's real.

waysIn.title: Create room for the real answer
waysIn.description: Ask in a way that clearly signals you want the real answer, not the easy one, and be ready to receive whatever that is without reacting badly.
waysIn.action: Ask a direct question and explicitly say you want the honest answer, not the polite one.

templates.title: performing, even off the clock
templates.description: They've been feeling like they're putting on a version of themselves for other people, even in situations where they could just relax and be real.

waysIn.tag: Give Permission To Drop The Act
waysIn.title: Make it explicitly safe to not perform
waysIn.description: Tell them directly that they don't need to perform with you, rather than assuming they already know that.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that they don't have to be "on" around you, ever.

templates.title: decision made, zero regrets
templates.description: They made a decision that had been weighing on them and feel genuinely settled about it, no lingering second-guessing after the fact.

waysIn.title: Don't reopen the question
waysIn.description: Support the decision without revisiting the pros and cons, reopening it now would undercut the peace they've found.
waysIn.action: Tell them you think they made the right call, and leave it there.

templates.title: went with the gut, it worked
templates.description: They made a choice by trusting their instinct rather than overanalyzing it, and having that instinct pay off is reinforcing their self-trust.

waysIn.title: Point out that their gut was right
waysIn.description: Name specifically that their instinct served them well here, reinforcing the value of trusting themselves next time too.
waysIn.action: Point out that their gut call turned out to be the right one.

templates.title: decision paralysis, activated
templates.description: They've been going back and forth between two choices without landing anywhere, and the indecision itself is starting to wear on them more than either option would.

waysIn.title: Support the process, not a side
waysIn.description: Resist the urge to tell them which option seems better, help them think it through without adding your own preference into the mix.
waysIn.action: Ask them to talk through what each option would actually feel like, without you weighing in on which is right.

templates.title: wondering if they picked wrong
templates.description: They've been replaying a decision they already made, wondering if they should have chosen differently, even though it can't be undone now.

waysIn.title: Bring focus to what's next, not what's past
waysIn.description: Dwelling on an unchangeable decision rarely helps, gently shift focus toward what can still be done now rather than relitigating the choice.
waysIn.action: Ask what, if anything, can still be adjusted going forward, rather than revisiting the original choice.

templates.title: putting off the choice, indefinitely
templates.description: They've been avoiding making a decision entirely, hoping it'll resolve itself or become clearer without them having to actually choose.

waysIn.title: Point out the delay without pressure
waysIn.description: Gently name that the decision is being avoided, without pushing them to decide, sometimes just naming it is enough to shift something.
waysIn.action: Ask what's making the decision feel too hard to face.

templates.subScenario: Feeling Good In Their Own Lane
templates.title: unbothered by everyone else's timeline
templates.description: They've been feeling genuinely at peace with their own pace and progress, less pulled into comparing their path to anyone else's.

waysIn.title: Celebrate their specific journey
waysIn.description: Reinforce this mindset by praising their specific path rather than comparing them favorably to anyone else, which would undercut the point.
waysIn.action: Point out something about their journey that's uniquely theirs.

templates.subScenario: Inspired Rather Than Threatened by Others' Success
templates.title: someone else's win, feeling motivated instead
templates.description: Seeing someone else succeed lit them up rather than making them feel behind, and that shift in reaction is a genuinely healthy one.

waysIn.title: Name the healthier reaction
waysIn.description: Point out this reaction as the growth it is, since it would have been easy to feel threatened instead.
waysIn.action: Tell them you noticed how they reacted to that, and that it says something good about them.

templates.title: everyone's ahead, apparently
templates.description: They've been measuring themselves against peers and feeling like they're falling behind, even without clear evidence that's actually true.

waysIn.title: Question whose timeline this even is
waysIn.description: Gently question the comparison itself rather than reassuring them they're not behind, since the whole framing may be the problem.
waysIn.action: Ask who specifically they're comparing themselves to, and whether that comparison is even fair.

templates.tag: Someone Else's Win, Feels Like Their Loss
templates.title: happy for them, sad for themselves
templates.description: Someone else's good news has left them feeling smaller by comparison, a mix of genuine happiness for the other person and quiet discouragement about themselves.

waysIn.title: Don't dismiss the complicated mix
waysIn.description: Let both feelings be valid at once, being happy for someone and feeling discouraged for yourself aren't contradictory, don't push them to pick one.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's okay to feel both things at the same time.

templates.title: comparison brain, permanently on
templates.description: They've been in a near-constant habit of measuring themselves against other people, and the mental exhaustion of it is starting to wear them down.

waysIn.title: Anchor them back to themselves
waysIn.description: Help redirect their focus to their own personal progress rather than an external benchmark that keeps shifting.
waysIn.action: Ask them what winning looks like by their own definition, not anyone else's.

templates.title: guard down, on purpose
templates.description: They've been letting their guard down more than usual, feeling safe enough to be a little more open and unguarded than their default.

waysIn.title: Handle it with care
waysIn.description: This openness is a bit fragile, handle whatever they share gently so the instinct to guard up again doesn't return.
waysIn.action: Thank them for being more open, without making a big deal that draws attention to the shift itself.

templates.title: trusting people a little faster lately
templates.description: They've noticed themselves extending trust more readily than usual, less bracing for disappointment, more giving people the benefit of the doubt.

waysIn.title: Match it with reliability
waysIn.description: This shift deserves to be met with consistency, follow through on the small things so the trust they're extending keeps feeling justified.
waysIn.action: Follow through on something small you said you'd do, without needing to be reminded.

templates.title: guard: fully up
templates.description: They've been more emotionally closed off than usual, keeping people, including those close to them, at more of a distance.

waysIn.title: Stay steady without pushing
waysIn.description: Pushing for openness usually backfires, stay reliably present without demanding they open up before they're ready.
waysIn.action: Let them know you're there without asking them to explain the distance.

templates.title: trust: running low
templates.description: They've been finding it harder to trust, bracing for letdown even in situations that haven't given them a reason to expect one.

waysIn.title: Let actions rebuild it slowly
waysIn.description: Trust rebuilds through repeated small reliability, not reassurance, focus on consistent follow-through rather than telling them to trust more.
waysIn.action: Do exactly what you say you'll do, even in something small, without drawing attention to it.

templates.title: said no, felt fine about it
templates.description: They set a boundary they'd normally struggle to hold, and instead of the usual guilt, they've felt genuinely at peace with it.

waysIn.title: Honor it without pushing back
waysIn.description: Reinforce this growth by respecting the boundary completely, any pushback here would undo the confidence they just built.
waysIn.action: Tell them you respect that they set the boundary, and mean it.

templates.title: chose themselves, no apology
templates.description: They made a choice that prioritized their own needs over automatically accommodating someone else, and it's clearly felt like a healthy shift.

waysIn.title: Reinforce it as a good thing
waysIn.description: Frame this as growth rather than selfishness, since the instinct to feel guilty about it may still be lingering underneath.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's good to see them putting themselves first for once.

templates.title: said yes, meant no
templates.description: They agreed to something they didn't actually want to, unable to say no even when it clearly wasn't good for them.

waysIn.title: Show them saying no is fine with you
waysIn.description: Explicitly tell them it's okay to say no to you specifically, since they may be extending the same people-pleasing pattern here too.
waysIn.action: Tell them directly that they're allowed to say no to you without it being a problem.

templates.title: giving until there's nothing left
templates.description: They've been giving so much of their time and energy to other people that there's little left over for themselves.

waysIn.tag: Give Them Permission To Pull Back
waysIn.title: Actively encourage less giving
waysIn.description: Actively encourage them to do less for others, rather than just sympathizing with how tired they are.
waysIn.action: Take something off their plate that they'd normally do for someone else.

templates.title: said no, still feeling bad about it
templates.description: They set a boundary but are now feeling guilty about it, second-guessing whether they had the right to say no in the first place.

waysIn.title: Affirm the boundary was fair
waysIn.description: Directly affirm that the boundary was reasonable, countering the guilt rather than staying neutral about whether it was justified.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that the boundary was fair and they didn't do anything wrong.

templates.title: set the guilt down, finally
templates.description: They let go of guilt they'd been carrying for a while, and the relief of no longer holding onto it is noticeably lightening their mood.

waysIn.title: Reinforce it's genuinely behind them
waysIn.description: Affirm that it's truly okay to have let this go, rather than leaving room for the guilt to creep back in.
waysIn.action: Tell them you're glad they've let that go, and that they don't need to carry it anymore.

templates.title: apologized, meant it, moved on
templates.description: They took responsibility for something and made it right, and there's real relief in having actually resolved it instead of just feeling bad about it.

waysIn.title: Recognize the accountability it took
waysIn.description: Point out that taking responsibility like that isn't easy, name the maturity in how they handled it.
waysIn.action: Tell them it took guts to make that right, and that you noticed.

templates.title: guilt, still unpacked
templates.description: They've been holding onto guilt about something without having resolved it, and it's quietly weighing on them more than they're letting on.

waysIn.title: Open the door without forcing it
waysIn.description: Create a low-pressure opening for them to address what's weighing on them, rather than letting it sit unspoken indefinitely.
waysIn.action: Ask if there's something they've been sitting with that they'd want to talk through.

templates.title: hiding something from themselves too
templates.description: They've been carrying shame about something, more than ordinary guilt, feeling like it reflects badly on who they are as a person.

waysIn.tag: Separate The Act From Their Character
waysIn.title: Draw the line between what they did and who they are
waysIn.description: Explicitly separate the action from their character, since shame conflates the two in a way that guilt doesn't.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that one thing they did doesn't define who they are.

templates.subScenario: Overblown Guilt Over a Small Thing
templates.title: guilt-tripping themselves over nothing much
templates.description: They've been feeling disproportionately guilty about something relatively minor, holding onto it with more weight than the situation actually calls for.

waysIn.title: Put the guilt back in proportion
waysIn.description: Gently point out the mismatch between how minor the thing was and how heavy they're treating it, without dismissing that it still matters to them.
waysIn.action: Tell them plainly that this really isn't as big a deal as it feels.

templates.title: finally put the grudge down
templates.description: They let go of resentment they'd been holding onto, and the lightness of no longer carrying that anger around is a genuine relief.

waysIn.title: Don't reopen the old grievance
waysIn.description: Avoid bringing up the old situation even in passing, protect the peace they've found by leaving it fully in the past.
waysIn.action: Tell them it's good to see them lighter, without referencing what they let go of.

templates.subScenario: Processed Anger in a Healthy Way
templates.title: got mad, handled it well
templates.description: They felt genuinely angry about something and worked through it constructively instead of suppressing it or letting it fester.

waysIn.title: Point out how well they processed it
waysIn.description: Acknowledge specifically how well they moved through the anger, reinforcing that expressing it in a healthy way is a good thing, not something to hide.
waysIn.action: Tell them you noticed how well they handled being upset about that.

templates.title: resentment, simmering quietly
templates.description: They've been holding onto resentment about something without addressing it directly, and it's been quietly building under the surface.

waysIn.tag: Create An Opening To Address It
waysIn.title: Invite it out into the open
waysIn.description: Gently invite whatever's underneath to surface, since unaddressed resentment tends to grow rather than fade on its own.
waysIn.action: Ask if something's been bothering them that they haven't fully said out loud.

templates.title: mad, but not saying it
templates.description: They've been holding back anger they clearly feel, choosing to stay quiet rather than express what's actually upsetting them.

waysIn.tag: Make Anger Feel Safe To Express
waysIn.title: Show it's okay to be upset with you
waysIn.description: Explicitly signal that their anger, even directed at you, is safe to express, rather than assuming they know that already.
waysIn.action: Tell them directly that it's okay to tell you when they're upset, and mean it.

templates.title: small things, big reactions
templates.description: Their reactions to minor annoyances have been bigger than usual, a sign that something larger is likely sitting underneath the surface irritation.

waysIn.title: Address the real source, not the small spark
waysIn.description: The small thing they snapped at is probably not the real issue, gently ask about what's actually underneath rather than reacting to the surface trigger.
waysIn.action: Ask what's really been bothering them lately, separate from whatever just triggered the reaction.

templates.title: grateful they picked this person
templates.description: They've had a wave of appreciation for you wash over them, unprompted by any one moment, just a settled sense of gratitude for having you in their life.

waysIn.title: Let the appreciation land
waysIn.description: Meet this gratitude with your own, rather than deflecting it, let it be a mutual moment instead of brushing it off.
waysIn.action: Tell your partner something specific you're grateful for about them.

templates.title: crushing on their own partner
templates.description: They've had a sudden resurgence of the early-relationship kind of excitement about you, out of nowhere and clearly delightful to them.

waysIn.title: Lean into the renewed excitement
waysIn.description: This is a good moment to be a little extra, matching their energy rather than treating the relationship as routine.
waysIn.action: Do something a little flirtatious or unexpected to keep the spark going.

templates.title: future with them, feeling certain
templates.description: They've been feeling a real, settled confidence about where the relationship is headed, less uncertainty, more trust in the long-term picture.

waysIn.title: Speak to the future together
waysIn.description: Reinforce this confidence by talking about the future together in concrete terms, rather than staying vague about what's ahead.
waysIn.action: Bring up something specific you're looking forward to together down the line.

templates.tag: Proud Of How Far You've Come
templates.title: relationship glow-up noticed
templates.description: They've been reflecting on how much the relationship has grown and improved over time, and feeling genuinely proud of what they've built with you.

waysIn.title: Acknowledge the growth mutually
waysIn.description: Take a moment to genuinely reflect on the relationship's growth with them, rather than letting the observation go unacknowledged.
waysIn.action: Bring up something specific about how the relationship has gotten better over time.

templates.title: wondering if this is right
templates.description: They've been quietly questioning whether the relationship is truly right for them, more uncertainty than crisis, but it's been sitting with them.

waysIn.title: Don't panic, invite honesty instead
waysIn.description: This isn't a moment to get defensive or panic, create a calm, non-judgmental space for them to voice what's underneath the doubt.
waysIn.action: Ask gently if something's been on their mind about the relationship, and really listen without getting defensive.

templates.subScenario: Feeling Distant Without a Clear Cause
templates.title: feels far, can't say why
templates.description: They've noticed a sense of distance in the relationship without pointing to any specific cause, a diffuse feeling that something's slightly off.

waysIn.title: Close the gap through presence, not questions
waysIn.description: Rather than demanding to know exactly what's wrong, focus on creating genuine closeness and let the distance close naturally.
waysIn.action: Plan real, undistracted time together with no agenda beyond reconnecting.

templates.title: not sure what's ahead for us
